papers.summary: Active distribution networks increasingly rely on coordinated inverter-based resources to accommodate renewable generation, while harmonic limits constrain the capacity that can be connected. This paper proposes a harmonic optimal power flow (HOPF) method with active energy-storage-system (ESS) support. ESS charging, discharging and harmonic-current compensation are jointly scheduled under state-of-charge dynamics and a shared converter-current rating. An adaptive decision tree learns voltage-current partitions from OPF operating points. Within each leaf, an affine plane is fitted on an analytic grid and certified as a lower envelope. A disaggregated mixed-integer formulation embeds these envelopes in a second-order-cone-relaxed network model. Annual hourly data are assessed through daily capacity optimization, followed by componentwise capacity aggregation and chronological full-year feasibility validation. In the case study, the OPF reference of 65.572 MW exceeds the adopted harmonic bounds, whereas HOPF without harmonic support yields an annually validated capacity of 56.892 MW. With each generator capacity bounded by its OPF reference, the proposed method recovers the complete reference allocation. Coordinated energy dispatch and harmonic compensation thus recover generation capacity within the installed ESS converter ratings.

papers.title: No Supersoft X-rays Before SN 2026ahvu: Constraints on a Potentially Prompt Type Ia Progenitor
papers.summary: The nearby Type Ia supernova SN 2026ahvu offers a rare opportunity to probe its progenitor that may have evolved unusually rapidly. If the progenitor formed in either of the two young stellar clusters near the explosion site in NGC 1433, the delay from star formation to explosion could have been $\sim$100 Myr or less. The distance to NGC 1433 remains uncertain, with published estimates of 9.1 Mpc and 18.9 Mpc. Our preliminary fit to the rising ATLAS light curve yields a distance of $17.7^{+1.5}_{-1.4}$ Mpc. In the classical single-degenerate scenario, a white dwarf steadily burning hydrogen accreted from a non-degenerate companion can emit detectable supersoft X-rays before explosion. We search for this emission using two archival Chandra observations obtained before the explosion. The observations provide a combined exposure of 95.3 ks, with no 0.3-7 keV photons detected within 2" of the supernova position. For a 100 eV blackbody with Galactic foreground absorption, the 95\% bolometric luminosity limits are $6.3\times10^{37}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and $2.7\times10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ at 9.1 Mpc and 18.9 Mpc, respectively. At both distances, the observations exclude a hot, compact white dwarf undergoing steady hydrogen burning if the absorption is limited to the Galactic foreground. However, cooler, expanded, or more heavily absorbed photospheres remain viable. Together with the pre-explosion non-detections for SN 2011fe and SN 2014J, our results reinforce the absence of luminous supersoft progenitors in nearby SNe Ia. This pattern is naturally consistent with double-degenerate explosions, although X-ray-faint single-degenerate configurations remain viable. Post-explosion X-ray observations can test for circumstellar interaction and help determine whether material around the progenitor could have obscured a luminous nuclear burning white dwarf.

papers.title: Quantum adiabatic and diabatic optimization: A Hilbert space engineering strategy with Rydberg arrays
papers.summary: Neutral-atom arrays provide a versatile platform for encoding combinatorial optimization problems with arbitrary graph connectivity [Nguyen et al., PRX Quantum 4, 010316 (2023)]. Although the dynamics of individual encoding gadgets has been studied [Bombieri et al., PRX Quantum 6, 020306 (2025)], understanding annealing bottlenecks in larger networks remains challenging. We investigate how engineering the Hilbert-space geometry controls quantum annealing in a family of blockaded-chain models motivated by these encodings. While boundary terms encode the target maximum independent set problem, the bulk geometry induces an auxiliary optimization problem associated with independent sets of cliques. Spectrally, the energetics of the quantum system can be approximated by physically derived clique weights. When the target problem and the auxiliary problems are consistent, the low-energy modes lie predominantly within the target subspace. This spectral structure motivates a diabatic annealing strategy that exploits target-compatible excited states, as tested on the diamond-chain graph family. These results provide a framework for predicting annealing bottlenecks, and demonstrate Hilbert-space engineering as a strategy for improving neutral-atom quantum optimization protocols.

papers.title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
papers.summary: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference. We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF), which jointly denoises chunks at progressive noise levels with bidirectional attention within each window and causal access to preceding history. To retain historical context efficiently, hierarchical KV-cache compression (HieraKV) exploits layer-wise attention patterns, retaining full history in shallow layers and sink--recent history in deeper layers. This reduces cache memory by up to 78% while improving generation quality. Building on this base, cumulative long tuning with distribution matching distillation (CuLT-DMD) holds parameters fixed throughout each long self-rollout and averages local gradients before updating. Each update therefore combines supervision across temporal positions while retaining only one local computation graph, enabling efficient long-rollout training of a few-step generator. To extend generation beyond the training horizon, KV recomputation bounds context for both models, while guidance annealing (AnnealCFG) reduces guidance toward the clean endpoint to stabilize MovieRoll-Base. Complementing these modeling advances, FBCA attention and PS-VAE decoding support efficient training and streaming output. On HeliosBench, MovieRoll-Base remains competitive at 30s after training on videos of up to 15s, and MovieRoll-Distilled achieves the highest total scores among the compared methods across single- and multi-event evaluations up to 60s, combining sustained naturalness with active motion.

papers.title: Generating a simple silicon detector simulation with an open-weight large language model
papers.summary: Recent LLM developments have seen AI-generated code become commonplace in the software development industry. Without tool access, LLMs cannot execute simulations, and their knowledge of toolkits such as Geant4 is limited. We demonstrate here, a detector simulation workflow with a Qwen3.6-27B model with Q4_K_M GGUF quantisation together with custom resources and tools served via MCP servers to generate a particle detector simulation. In 50 independent runs, 42(29--56)% at 95% CI produced energy-deposit distributions statistically consistent with a reference simulation, measured against a reference simulation. These results provide a proof of concept that MC simulations can be generated using text-based prompts with an LLM, given the necessary resources and tools. More extensive resources, such as example code and additional documentation, are likely to be required for more complex simulation tasks.

papers.title: On the origin of Milky Way binary black holes with LISA
papers.summary: Primordial black holes (PBHs) may constitute a fraction of dark matter, but distinguishing them from black holes of stellar origin remains a major challenge. We propose a new method based on the three-dimensional localization of Galactic Binary Black Holes (BBHs) by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). While stellar-origin BBHs are expected to be associated with the stellar distribution of the Milky Way, PBHs may trace its more extended dark matter halo. We introduce a spatial overlap ratio that compares the gravitational-wave localization of each binary with the normalized stellar and dark matter density profiles. Using a Fisher-matrix forecast and 1000 Monte Carlo realizations of a 10-year LISA mission, we find that detecting three BBHs with an overlap ratio ln B < 0 occurs in approximately 99% of simulations where BBHs trace dark matter, but in fewer than 0.1% of simulations where they follow the stellar distribution, even when including a stellar halo containing 3% of the Galactic stellar mass. These results suggest that the localization of only a few Galactic BBHs could provide strong evidence for a primordial population, offering an independent test of their possible contribution to dark matter.

papers.title: Why Cassini's Oval Could Not Replace Kepler's Ellipse?
papers.summary: In the later seventeenth century, Kepler's ellipse was not yet accepted. Ward claimed that Boulliau's conic hypothesis amounted to a Ptolemaic equant at the ellipse's empty focus, and built his own model on it. Around 1675--1680, Giovanni Domenico Cassini proposed another curve, the ``oval'', a genus-1 quartic with no closed-form Kepler equation; yet its eccentric anomaly shares exactly the leading coefficient of Kepler's, and its empty focus is, for the Sun, 38 times closer to a true equant than the ellipse's. Dynamically, Binet's formula shows that the force producing the oval under the area law departs from the inverse square by an index $\mathcal{D}(e)\sim3/(4e^2)$, depending on the oval's parameter $e$: no single exponent serves the whole family. This absence of universality, not of an area law, distinguishes it from the ellipse, and arguably explains why Cassini, the Académie and Leibniz kept the question open after the \emph{Principia} (1687).

papers.title: Anchoring Motion, Refining Trajectories: Generalizable Continuous Neural Decoding
papers.summary: Brain activity encodes motor information across multiple temporal scales, enabling continuous neural control beyond discrete action recognition. However, existing methods are typically tailored to specific subjects and tasks, with direct neural-to-kinematic mappings that can entangle subject-specific neural variability with task-dependent motion patterns, limiting generalization. To address these limitations, we introduce AMRT, a shared neural decoding framework for heterogeneous electrode configurations and movement paradigms. Motivated by cortical encoding of movement direction and speed, AMRT adopts a two-stage design that anchors local motion through velocity estimation and refines the resulting trajectories over longer horizons, encouraging reuse of local motion tendencies across subjects and tasks. Across three datasets, AMRT generalizes to unseen trials and subjects and demonstrates transfer potential across neural recordings and movement paradigms, highlighting the potential of shared neural representations and anchor-and-refine decoding for generalizable continuous neural control.

papers.title: Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
papers.summary: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations. Their Lax operators are obtained by restricting the corresponding products of linear oscillator Lax operators to these submodules. We determine the vacuum eigenvalues and Drinfeld polynomials, and give a determinant formula for the dimensions directly in terms of the highest loop weights. A $21$-dimensional example illustrates the construction, including an explicit basis and a transfer-matrix identity.

papers.title: Experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity in discrete time crystals
papers.summary: Discrete time crystals (DTCs) are almost always analyzed under the Born-Markov approximation, in which the environment is memoryless. We show that a reservoir with a finite correlation time $τ_m$ leaves an exact and strikingly simple imprint on the stroboscopic dynamics of DTCs, which can be used as an experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity. By analyzing a post-Markovian master equation we prove that the Floquet spectrum splits into the ordinary Markovian spectrum plus a replica of the purely unitary Floquet spectrum, uniformly contracted by $e^{-T/τ_m}$, where $T$ is the drive period. Consequently, the DTC signal decay rate becomes independent of any system parameter once $τ_m$ exceeds the Markovian lifetime of the DTC. The measured decay, and in particular its insensitivity to tunable system parameters, thus becomes a direct read-out of the reservoir correlation time. Below this threshold the dynamics is already non-Markovian, but the memory remains hidden in the decay. We confirm this in two structurally unrelated DTCs, a collective long-range model with incoherent pumping and a disorder-free Ising chain with dephasing, where a single estimator recovers $τ_m$. The time crystal thereby witnesses the non-Markovianity of its own environment.

papers.title: TRIAGE-CPG: A Cross-Model Study of Budgeted Static Malware Triage with Large Language Models
papers.summary: When triaging unknown binaries, security analysts must decide which samples to clear as benign, flag as malicious, or escalate for deeper analysis. Large Language Models (LLMs) could support these decisions by interpreting decompiled code, but a binary can contain hundreds or thousands of functions, making exhaustive LLM analysis impractical. We study how current LLMs behave when static triage is formulated as budgeted evidence acquisition: which functions they inspect and how they trade off benign clearance, malware detection, and escalation. To enable a controlled comparison, we implement TRIAGE-CPG, a fixed pipeline over a code property graph (CPG) of a decompiled binary. An LLM-free heuristic selects seed functions, an agent expands the resulting evidence dossier under a fixed budget, and a reporting stage produces a benign, suspicious, or malicious verdict together with a behavioral report. We evaluate eight closed-source and open-weight models on 1,000 Windows PE binaries, using a 600-sample test split and the same zero-shot protocol for every model. We assess the ternary verdicts under both a strict binary reading and triage balanced accuracy (tBA), which credits malware that is flagged or escalated and benign samples only when cleared. After analyzing about 40 of a mean 1,000 functions per binary, the highest-scoring model reaches a strict balanced accuracy of 0.805 and a tBA of 0.855, flagging 65% of malware, escalating another 12%, and clearing 94% of benign samples. The models implement different triage policies: high-specificity models produce small, malware-rich escalation queues, whereas recall-oriented models escalate or flag much more broadly. Both closed-source and open-weight models appear across this spectrum. Our results identify no universal deployment configuration: model choice itself determines the clear/flag/escalate trade-off under limited static evidence.
papers.comment: Code and artifacts available here: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22771897
papers.journal: Proceedings of the 19th ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security (AISec '26), Association for Computing Machinery, New York, NY, USA, 2026, pp. 339-351

papers.title: tsspiral: An R Package to Create Circular Versions of Time Series Plots
papers.summary: `tsspiral` is an open-source R package that introduces a circular approach to time series visualisation using polar coordinates. We refer to this circular representation of time series data as a spiral. `tsspiral` provides a collection of `ggplot2` geometries for creating a spiral representation of time series data. In our approach, we arrange observations around a circle. Each year is represented by a circle, with the angular position corresponding to the day of the year, and successive years appear as concentric rings. This arrangement facilitates the exploration of periodicity, seasonality, and recurring temporal patterns, particularly in long time series. The package also supports temporal hierarchical visualisations to compare patterns across time scales. By bringing polar-coordinate-based visualisation into routine time series analysis, `tsspiral` offers a practical tool for exploring temporal patterns and communicating complex time-dependent structures. Rather than treating spiral plots as standalone graphics, our approach brings them into the grammar of graphics framework, enabling users to explore temporal patterns through a broader range of visual encodings.

papers.title: Neural Marked Point Processes for Health Insurance Claims
papers.summary: Health insurance claims exhibit temporal dependence, as previous claims may provide information about the timing, type and amount of subsequent claims. Such dependencies are difficult to capture with traditional actuarial models based on aggregated claim counts. We investigate a neural marked point process in which a causal Transformer represents individual claim histories and determines type-specific conditional intensities, allowing for self-excitation and interactions between claim types. The framework also incorporates conditional severity distributions, reporting delays and stochastic medical-cost inflation. We develop a likelihood-based calibration procedure that accounts for incomplete claim reporting and evaluate the model using both simulated and empirical data. A simulation study with 10,000 insurance contracts examines the recovery of known claim dynamics, while an application to MEPS-derived medical-event data assesses predictive performance. The fitted model reproduces the main patterns in claim frequencies and severities, although some discrepancies remain in the tails of the distributions. On the MEPS data, the neural model achieves better predictive performance than two generalized linear model benchmarks in terms of claim-count deviance and expenditure discrimination.

papers.title: Detectability of Eccentric Intermediate Mass-Ratio Inspiral in the Decihertz Band
papers.summary: The proposed decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) band $(\sim 10^{-2}-1\,\Hz)$ will observe the late inspiral of intermediate mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs), binaries with mass ratios $10^2 \lesssim q \lesssim 10^4$ that assemble dynamically in dense stellar environments and are expected to retain measurable eccentricity. Search and parameter-estimation pipelines are predominantly built around circular templates, and we test this assumption. Using black-hole perturbation theory waveforms from \textsc{FastEMRIWaveforms} for a representative IMRI ($M=10^4\,\modot$, $q=100$, observed for its final $10\,\hr$), we compute fitting factors between eccentric signals and circular templates, maximizing over the template's total mass and mass ratio with a differential-evolution search, for the B-DECIGO, LGWA-Si, and IndIGO-D noise curves and a flat PSD. The mismatch grows with initial eccentricity $e_0$ and crosses the standard $3\%$ threshold at $e_0\simeq3\times10^{-2}$, well within the range allowed by the waveform model and expected from dynamical formation. The best-fitting circular templates also bias the total mass and mass ratio by several percent at $e_0=0.1$. Combining the mismatch with the signal-to-noise-dependent distinguishability criterion, we find that for a source at $1\,\mathrm{Gpc}$, eccentricities as small as $e_0\simeq5\times10^{-4}$ (B-DECIGO and IndIGO-D) and $5\times10^{-3}$ (LGWA-Si) are resolvable, one to two orders of magnitude below where detection efficiency degrades. The loss of match arises from the excitation of radial Teukolsky harmonics, which spread power into sidebands that circular templates cannot represent, and from the slower orbital decay of eccentric binaries at fixed initial semi-latus rectum. Robust detection and parameter estimation of IMRIs with DECIGO, LGWA, and IndIGO-D will require eccentric waveform models and template banks.

papers.title: TCBP-JOBS: GPU-Accelerated Quantum Error Correction Decoding and Noise Learning with Near-Optimal Accuracy
papers.summary: Achieving near-optimal quantum error correction (QEC) decoding accuracy often requires computationally expensive searches that limit both large-scale simulation and real-time operation. We introduce trajectory-calibrated belief propagation (TCBP), which learns calibrated fault probabilities from BP trajectories, and jittered OSD beam search (JOBS), which uses these probabilities to guide parallel GPU searches. Across surface, color and bivariate-bicycle code memory and surgery circuits, TCBP-JOBS achieves logical error rates comparable to those of the Tesseract most-likely-error decoder at physical error rates of 0.1% to 0.4%, and up to 4.5$\times$ lower on the largest codes. Serial speedups over Tesseract's sparsified presets range from 10$\times$ to 7,400$\times$, and against unsparsified long-beam Tesseract they reach 13,000$\times$ on the bivariate-bicycle codes, at logical error rate ratios of 0.97 to 1.57. At lower physical error rates ($10^{-4}$ to $5\times10^{-4}$), rare-event splitting on the gross code shows that Tesseract is more accurate. Batched execution accelerates offline simulation for rapid, efficient exploration of large-scale QEC design spaces. For QPUs with longer logical clock cycles, our serial memory and logical-surgery experiments demonstrate accuracy comparable to Tesseract while meeting the millisecond-scale latency requirements of online feed-forward operation. Beyond memory and logic decoding, we demonstrate using TCBP-JOBS for confidence scores for postselection in memory and magic-state cultivation, enabling end-to-end color code cultivation. Together, these methods provide a GPU framework for accelerating QEC research via accurate decoding, noise estimation, and confidence assessment.

papers.title: Non-thermal emission from molecular clouds illuminated by continuous cosmic-ray accelerators: application to the stellar cluster W43
papers.summary: Context: Cosmic rays escaping from their accelerators produce gamma-ray emission through interactions with ambient gas. While the scenario of an impulsive injection of cosmic rays has been extensively studied, that of a continuous injection in time has received comparatively less attention. The latter scenario is particularly relevant for stellar clusters, which may contribute to a non-negligible fraction of Galactic cosmic rays. Aims: We intend to characterize the excesses of cosmic rays around their accelerators and to assess the detectability of the gamma-ray emission resulting from the interactions of cosmic rays in nearby molecular clouds. We focus in particular on star clusters and seek to apply these considerations to the case of W43. Methods: We derive analytical estimates for the cosmic ray excess around sources as a function of source properties and transport parameters. We also evaluate under which conditions the predicted gamma-ray emission from illuminated molecular clouds can be detected by current and future instruments. We then apply these results to explain the gamma-ray emission from the the W43 region. Results: We find that producing detectable gamma-ray emission from molecular clouds illuminated by cosmic rays escaping from star clusters generally requires either suppressed diffusion relative to the Galactic value or anisotropic diffusion, with the latter scenario requiring a smaller global energetic. We applied this approach to the case of W43 and by fitting its gamma-ray emission we were able to constrain the underlying CR transport parameters.

papers.title: Reference Replay for Excitation Injection and Subsequent Exponential Convergence under Concurrent Learning Adaptive Control
papers.summary: Concurrent learning (CL) guarantees precise identification of unknown parameters---if data with finite excitation (FE) happens to be collected online. To improve the reliability of CL, this work establishes a mechanism allowing FE-occurrence to be verified a priori: We propose replaying a given training segment in the reference until data with finite excitation is collected online. Provided the training segment fulfills a certain off-line excitation test, FE then occurs in unknown, but finite time. Moreover, we provide an upper bound on the time-to-FE. Even though this bound involves a dependency on the unknown initial Lyapunov-function value, its structure shows that FE occurs in arbitrarily early replay cycles when increasing the control gain; which may motivate employing a high-gain strategy. The theoretical findings are verified on an academic simulation example.

papers.title: Robust Optimal Network Reduction for Distribution Systems
papers.summary: Network reduction replaces large networks with smaller equivalents to speed up power flow and optimization studies. Optimal Kron-based Reduction of Networks (Opti-KRON) finds the optimal set of nodes to faithfully represent a large-scale radial network for representative loading scenarios. Under unseen nodal injections, however, its accuracy can drop. This paper extends Opti-KRON to uncertain nodal injections using robust uncertainty sets and a Wasserstein ambiguity set, with voltage magnitude error guarantees. To improve scalability, we develop a presolve screening step to eliminate redundant constraints and variables while preserving the feasible set. We also adopt adversarial constraint generation to reduce memory requirements by iteratively adding worst-case nodal injections. On a real 8,387-node feeder at a threshold of 0.001~p.u., the reduction removes 49.9% of the nodes. For one uncertainty set, adversarial constraint generation cuts the required memory by a factor of more than 18.

papers.title: A2A-UAV: A Multimodal Air-to-Air Dataset for UAV Detection and Identification
papers.summary: The rapid growth of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in low-altitude airspace increases the risk of unauthorized intrusions, making reliable detection and identification of non-cooperative UAVs essential for low-altitude airspace safety. However, the existing public UAV datasets are mostly acquired from fixed ground-based viewpoints and are limited to imaging or radio-frequency (RF) observations, which restricts the sensing coverage and deployment flexibility. To address this gap, we present A2A-UAV, a multimodal air-to-air dataset for UAV detection and identification. Specifically, 15 target UAVs of 13 commercial models were recorded at three outdoor sites under daytime and nighttime conditions by using a UAV-mounted platform equipped with an RGB-thermal gimbal camera, a panoramic camera, an RF spectrum analyzer, and a millimeter-wave radar. The dataset contains 105,294 time-aligned samples of RGB, panoramic, thermal, and RF time-frequency images and radar point clouds. Moreover, all 209,539 bounding boxes of the predominantly small UAV targets were manually annotated and cross-checked. Therefore, A2A-UAV provides a valuable resource for air-to-air UAV detection, identification, and multimodal fusion in low-altitude airspace.

papers.title: Safe Physical Interaction of All-Electric Heavy-Duty Robotic Manipulators via Control Barrier Functions and Variable Impedance Control
papers.summary: All-electric heavy-duty robotic manipulators are increasingly expected to operate close to tunnel walls, equipment, and other structures while retaining the force capability required for large-payload tasks. Accurate motion control alone does not address the resulting safety and interaction requirements. This paper develops a safety-aware physical-interaction architecture that combines variable impedance control (VIC) with control barrier functions (CBFs) on top of an established virtual decomposition control (VDC) framework for electromechanical linear actuator (EMLA)-driven manipulators. VIC continuously adapts the task-space stiffness and damping according to predicted proximity and contact risk, whereas a joint-velocity CBF filter enforces Cartesian workspace boundaries and the physical stroke limits induced by the closed-chain lift and tilt mechanisms. To account for nonideal realization of the filtered velocity by the inner VDC/EMLA dynamics, the CBF inequalities are tightened using a measured bound on the joint-velocity tracking error. Four configurations, namely VDC, VIC+VDC, CBF+VDC, and VIC+CBF+VDC, are evaluated under workspace, actuator-limit, and physical-interaction scenarios. VIC reduces the peak and RMS environment-interaction forces by 92.59% and 96.33%, respectively; both robust CBF configurations maintain positive workspace and EMLA safety margins, while VIC+CBF+VDC reduces the CBF intervention metric by 10.30% compared with CBF+VDC.

papers.title: Share your Screen and Talk to Gemini: How Young Learners Interact with Multimodal GenAI While Solving Scratch Tasks
papers.summary: Children using Scratch to learn programming can struggle with text-heavy, lengthy explanations and hints during debugging. Verbal interactions based on screen sharing or camera data may be an interesting alternative for supporting learners. We therefore explore the quality, use, and perceptions of fifth- and sixth-graders' verbal interactions with a GenAI tutor. The goal is to investigate the quality and use of the multimodal GenAI tutor in the given context. First of all, a pilot study of eight tasks conducted without students helped inform the process of the tutor's classroom evaluation. The classroom study was realized after fifth- and sixth-graders had participated in six Scratch classroom lessons. Then 23 students were introduced to the tutor, worked on the eight tasks with the GenAI tutor, and completed a questionnaire. The analysis of the pilot and classroom study shows that the tutor's responses were intelligible and actionable, and no single turn revealed a complete solution. However, the tutor missed existing errors in 61.5% of 603 error-related classroom turns, compared to 15.7% in the pilot study. Children's voice prompts were brief and mostly responded to the tutor. Although a video had explained that responses could be incorrect, 39.1% of the children trusted the tutor's answers to always be correct. These findings have implications for educators and learners using multimodal GenAI tutors, as they need to be aware that an intelligible and human-like voice does not ensure correct support. For developers, our results suggest that screen sharing alone does not ensure responses that match the program state.
papers.comment: accepted for: The 21th WiPSCE Conference on Primary and Secondary Computing Education Research (WiPSCE 27)

papers.title: High-probability Uniform Mixing via Dobrushin Contraction and Accelerated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
papers.summary: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, since its invention and subsequent rise to widespread use, has been motivated by its ability to accelerate convergence to equilibrium compared to diffusive methods, both in terms of dependence on condition number and dimension. In the present work, we establish this acceleration simultaneously in both aspects for critically damped Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin with persistent uniforms. More precisely, for target measures $μ(dx)\propto e^{-U(x)}dx$ with $m$-strongly convex, $L$-gradient Lipschitz, and $L_H$-Frobenius Hessian Lipschitz potentials, we show that the method mixes to $\varepsilon$-accuracy in total variation using $\mathcal O\bigl((κ^{1/2}+L_H^{1/2}m^{-3/4})\,d^{1/4}\bigr)$ gradient evaluations up to logarithmic factors, both uniformly over starting points in domains of high equilibrium probability and from warm starts. The proof incorporates ideas from previous studies by Bou-Rabee and Chen et al. that show either aspect of acceleration separately, into novel coupling technology. This new coupling technology for general Markov chains extends earlier frameworks aimed at capturing fast local equilibration in the presence of slow global mixing. Specifically, via a weak-$(1,1)$ maximal inequality that follows from Hopf's maximal ergodic theorem, we uncover a stability mechanism in high-probability domains with respect to equilibrium. This enables straightforward localization to naturally arising domains of fast local mixing, and seamlessly fits broad local frameworks via Dobrushin contraction, Wasserstein contraction and local Harris' theorems. We develop the Dobrushin formulation.

papers.title: Syllable- and Word-Level Evaluation of Tibetan OCR
papers.summary: Optical character recognition (OCR) for Tibetan is evaluated predominantly by character error rate (CER). Tibetan marks syllable boundaries but does not mark word boundaries, so a word error rate requires a segmenter. This study evaluates nine recognizer configurations on typeset, woodblock and two handwritten script styles, alone and in combination, and reports syllable- and word-level error rates, to our knowledge the first for Tibetan OCR. The configurations span CTC models, TrOCR encoder-decoders with and without post-training quantization, and a vision-language model, and each is scored under CER, the syllable error rate (SER) and three segmented word error rates (SWER). CER ranks systems largely as the higher-level rates do (Kendall $τ\geq 0.833$), with one pair ordered oppositely. On the effect of joint training, CER and SER record significant changes of opposite sign in 7 of 64 comparisons. SER needs no segmenter and ranks systems as SWER does under two of the three segmenters ($τ\geq 0.889$). The output of each configuration is also tagged for part of speech, annotated for named entities and machine translated, and each result is compared with that obtained on the reference text. As rough guidance, translation chrF of 60 is reached at SER of 0.047 or below and part-of-speech preservation of 0.8 at 0.078 or below, while no error rate separates the systems that reach entity preservation of 0.6 from those that do not.

papers.title: Déjà-Events: Multi-view 3D Geometry with Event Cameras via Sparsity-Aware Adaptive Gating
papers.summary: Event cameras keep capturing structure where conventional cameras blur or saturate, which makes them attractive for 3D perception in fast or poorly lit scenes. Event datasets with dense 3D ground truth, however, are far smaller and less diverse than the image collections behind feed-forward 3D reconstruction models. We present Déjà-Events, an event-only model that predicts depth, camera pose and pointmaps from multiple views in a single forward pass. Rather than relying on scarce 3D labels, we distil it from Déjà View, a feed-forward RGB model that refines its tokens by repeatedly applying one shared transformer block. On paired RGB and event recordings, the event student learns to reproduce the frozen teacher's final tokens, which requires no depth or pose ground truth and trains only about 1% of its parameters. Because events are dense at edges and moving texture but nearly absent in textureless regions, we further introduce sparsity-aware adaptive gating, which adapts the shared block's gates to events and adjusts them per patch by event density, so that accuracy holds as refinement steps are added. Trained only on simulated data, Déjà-Events achieves the lowest pointmap error among the event-based methods we evaluate, on EventScape and zero-shot on the real MVSEC and DSEC datasets. On DSEC it halves the error of the strongest baseline (0.15 vs. 0.30 AbsRel) with about a tenth of its parameters. It also has the lowest depth error on EventScape and DSEC and the lowest trajectory error on EventScape.

papers.title: Latent Bridge: Asking for Help Without Words
papers.summary: Text-based model collaboration requires a large model to generate intermediate responses before a smaller model can use its guidance, adding large-model decoding cost to inference. We introduce POND (Prefill-Only, No-Decode), a method that uses a frozen large sender for prefill and a small receiver for all autoregressive decoding. A trainable bridge maps the sender's hidden states to additional attention keys and values, allowing the receiver to use these representations throughout generation. POND also supports periodic review, in which the sender processes the receiver's partial response and updates its guidance through additional prefill passes while preserving the receiver's existing KV cache. Across reasoning and coding benchmarks, POND improves receiver performance with senders from different model families. In particular, GLM-5.3 provides gains comparable to those of Qwen3.8-Max when paired with a Qwen receiver, supporting the effectiveness of representation transfer between independently trained model families. POND further demonstrates its ability to generalize across domains. When trained on math and coding tasks, it transfers directly to general knowledge tasks without additional domain-specific training. These results demonstrate that large frontier model prefill representations can improve small-model generation without requiring large-model autoregressive decoding.

papers.title: LATTE-WordSeg-Lite: Multi-Granularity Thai Word Segmentation on a CPU, with a Reproducible Benchmark
papers.summary: Large language models read Thai through subword tokens, without a word segmenter. Yet Thai treebanks, speech metrics and morphological resources are built on words, often at several granularities, and word boundaries resolve ambiguities that subword tokens leave open. LATTE (Lattice ATTentive Encoding) reads a text at several granularities at once, through a lattice of dictionary words, but it is a large GPU model. We distil it into LATTE-WordSeg-Lite, a CPU segmenter of 1.17M parameters that keeps the lattice as features. It outputs compounds, words and morphemes in one pass, and learns only from annotated data and text whose licences allow commercial use. To compare it with other tools, published Thai scores do not suffice, as they come from different files, splits and scorers. We therefore rebuild seven test sets from pinned sources and score twelve systems under one protocol. With the unit that fits each test set, LATTE-WordSeg-Lite scores above DeepCut on five sets, four of them from corpora that its teachers learnt from. Called line by line on one CPU thread, it runs 23 times as fast as DeepCut. We release the model, the benchmark scripts and all predictions.

papers.title: Lifting asymptotic symmetries from metric to tetrad formulation
papers.summary: Metric solution spaces defined by gauge and boundary conditions are associated with a residual symmetry algebra, consisting of the diffeomorphism generators whose action preserves these conditions. Describing a metric solution space in terms of tetrad variables adds a local Lorentz freedom. When part of this freedom is fixed by additional tetrad gauge and boundary conditions, metric residual symmetries must be supplemented by compensating Lorentz transformations. If a residual Lorentz freedom remains, there is an ambiguity in these compensating transformations. The most direct choices generally fail to realize the metric residual symmetry algebra as a subalgebra of the tetrad one, because of a field-dependent cocycle. We show that a reference tetrad, that is a section of the tetrad solution space seen as a principal bundle over the metric one, always provides a lift free of this cocycle, so that the tetrad residual symmetry algebra is the semi-direct sum of the metric one and the ideal of field-dependent residual Lorentz transformations. The construction is independent of the gauge conditions, of the residual group, of the first-order Lagrangian, and reduces to the Kosmann lift on metric isometry generators. We illustrate it on a Weyl BMS-type solution space with time-dependent boundary metric, described in tetrad variables with a residual U(1) Lorentz freedom, for which the cocycle of a naive lift is computed and then explicitly removed.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Physicists: From Linear Regression to Reasoning Models
papers.summary: These lecture notes are based on an introductory course on neural networks and deep learning that the author taught in the School of Mathematical Sciences at Queen Mary University of London in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The author, however, is a physicist, and it shows: wherever possible, ideas are explained with physical intuition rather than heavy formalism. Readers with a background in physics or mathematics who want a self-contained, introductory route into modern machine learning may therefore find these notes particularly friendly. The notes start from maximum likelihood, least squares, linear regression and (stochastic) gradient descent. They then cover neural networks, backpropagation, the vanishing gradient problem, batch and layer normalization, overfitting and regularization, adversarial examples, and the kernel method. The second half turns to natural language processing: word embeddings, recurrent networks and LSTMs, the attention mechanism and Transformers, and large language models, including scaling laws, the history of GPT, instruction tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, hallucination, alignment faking, chain-of-thought reasoning and test-time scaling. The emphasis on large language models reflects requests from the students. The notes are aimed at third- and fourth-year students in the UK system. Because the course was also taken by students from other departments, very little is assumed: even basic material such as matrix multiplication is explained from scratch, so readers familiar with it can safely skip such parts. No originality is claimed; the aim is a coherent, intuitive path through the material. Developments after spring 2025 are not covered, but the basic ideas emphasized here are unlikely to go out of date soon.
papers.comment: 115 pages, many figures. Based on lectures given at Queen Mary University of London

papers.title: AnachroBench: Evaluating Historical Consistency in Large Vision-Language Models
papers.summary: Existing Large Vision-Language Model benchmarks primarily evaluate visual understanding in general everyday scenarios, leaving historical consistency with a specified era and country largely underexplored. To address this gap, we propose AnachroBench, a controlled discriminative benchmark for evaluating historical consistency in visual scenes. It contains 1,600 image pairs from eight countries spanning the late 19th to the early 20th century, each pairing an original historical image with an anachronistic version containing a seamlessly inserted modern object. AnachroBench evaluates three aspects: Inserted Object Perception, which tests whether models detect the inserted modern object; Era-Country Consistency, which assesses whether the scene is consistent with the specified era and country; and Conditional Era-Country Consistency, which measures consistency judgments only when the inserted object is correctly perceived. A false consistency judgment occurs when a model perceives the modern object but still judges the scene as historically consistent. Overall, AnachroBench reveals a gap between inserted object perception and era-country consistency judgments, providing a targeted evaluation of this behavior.

papers.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Linguistic Annotation
papers.summary: Assessing large language models for linguistic annotation requires task-specific evaluation under documented conditions. We present dhAIBench, a Python benchmarking and annotation tool with a web interface for exploring and sharing results. It records prompts, configurations and predictions, enabling comparisons of annotation quality, confidence calibration, repeatability and estimated cost. We demonstrate the framework and the associated methodology through 293 runs of 48 models on nine linguistic annotation tasks spanning morphology, syntax, semantics, discourse-pragmatics, spelling normalization and learner-language correction. Models achieve high agreement with reference annotations on several tasks, including those on non-standardized, historical varieties as well as requiring contextual interpretation. The results support evaluating models against specific linguistic tasks, rather than relying on general rankings. To this end, we make the current and future benchmarks publicly available at dhaibench.silent3.ff.cuni.cz.

papers.title: Generalized transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions of a photon and orbital angular momentum
papers.summary: The coefficients of generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) that encode the canonical fermion orbital angular momentum and spin--orbit correlation do not contribute to the direct transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) and generalized-parton-distribution (GPD) projections. We present, to our knowledge, the first explicit calculation of the leading-twist, time-even, chiral-even fermion GTMDs of an on-shell real photon at zero skewness and order $α$. The coefficients $\mathcal{F}_A$ and $\mathcal{G}_A$, which multiply the $k_\perp\timesΔ_\perp$ structure, yield the fermion orbital angular momentum $\ell_z^f$ and spin--orbit correlation $\mathcal{C}_z^f$. For photon helicity $+1$, both are obtained in closed form in the leading fermion--antifermion sector and obey $\mathcal{C}_z^f=-\ell_z^f/2$ for a common transverse regulator independent of $x$, because the channel with the active fermion's spin anti-aligned with its orbital motion carries three times the integrated weight of the aligned channel. The projections reproduce the known photon TMDs and leading-logarithmic photon-to-fermion kernels, and energy-momentum-tensor overlaps reproduce the known one-loop photon gravitational form factors $F_1$, $F_2$, and $F_3$. Our result provides an analytic benchmark for fermionic orbital and spin--orbit structure in the real photon.

papers.title: Compressed Simulation-Based Inference: Neural Posterior Estimation for Massive Data via Low-Dimensional Sketches
papers.summary: Neural posterior estimation (NPE) is a popular Bayesian simulation-based inference (SBI) approach that uses neural networks trained on simulated data--parameter pairs to approximate the posterior given a user-chosen prior. For high-dimensional observations, NPE methods typically approximate the conditional density of the parameter given a user-chosen or learned summary statistic, rather than the entire dataset, due to the curse of dimensionality. However, both approaches face challenges: hand-crafting good summaries for complex models requires considerable effort from scientists, while learning them from massive datasets can be prohibitively computationally expensive. To address these challenges, we propose approximating the conditional density of a parameter given low-dimensional sketches of the data. We show that, for a model with a $p$-dimensional parameter, only $2p+1$ random sketches are needed for posterior consistency. We compare with state-of-the-art embedding networks for NPE, and we find that our method \emph{matches} the best embedding network's performance while \emph{increasing computational efficiency}.

papers.title: Third-body-corrected Two-Pion Femtoscopic Correlations in Au+Au Collisions at High Baryon Density
papers.summary: Identical charged pion femtoscopy provides a sensitive probe of the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in heavy-ion collisions. At high baryon density, the differences between $π^+π^+$ and $π^-π^-$ Hanbury Brown--Twiss (HBT) radii may originate from both the third-body Coulomb effect and the initial-state isospin asymmetry. Since the latter is related to the equation of state (EoS) of asymmetric nuclear matter, separating these two effects is essential. In these proceedings, we present the measurements of identical charged pion correlations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=3.0$, 3.2, 3.5, 3.9, 4.5, and 7.7 GeV collected by the STAR experiment. A correction procedure is developed to remove the residual third-body Coulomb effect. After correction, the extracted HBT radii of $π^+π^+$ and $π^-π^-$ become consistent within uncertainties. The results indicate that the observed charge dependence is dominated by the third-body Coulomb effect, while any remaining contribution from the initial-state isospin asymmetry to the relative HBT radius difference, $(R_{π^-}-R_{π^+})/R_{π^+}$, is constrained to be less than 5\% at the 95\% confidence level.

papers.title: PLECTA: Overlap-aware instance segmentation of dense strand networks from binary masks
papers.summary: Many materials and tissues, including carbon-nanotube sheets, collagen and paper, comprise overlapping strands whose arrangement influences their effective properties. Measuring this geometry from micrographs requires individual strands to be traced through crossings and signal gaps, which merge distinct strands or split one strand into disconnected fragments. We present PLECTA (from Latin plecta, a braid), a deterministic method that segments individual strands using only a binary image whose foreground pixels mark strand centrelines. At each junction, PLECTA selects which strand segments continue into one another while allowing segments to terminate. It formulates this decision as an exact maximum-weight partial-matching problem, with an explicit penalty for unpaired segments and no restriction on the number of segments entering a junction. The output permits crossing pixels to belong to multiple strands. On synthetic scenes, PLECTA resolved strand identities more accurately than three released alternatives at every density tested. The same ranking held on an independently published generator run at its own settings. A separate stage uses the corresponding greyscale micrograph to estimate which strand lies on top at each crossing. The complete workflow is demonstrated on scanning electron micrographs of carbon nanotube sheets, from raw images to individual strand instances with estimated crossing order, without manual annotations for training or as pipeline inputs.

papers.title: A database of optical and thermal-radiative behaviour of materials under solar radiation
papers.summary: Solar-matter interactions are important in many scientific and engineering applications. Modeling them needs consistent optical and thermal-radiative properties over the full solar spectrum. Here we present SpaderOptics, a database for 21 materials: metals, oxides, semiconductors, polymers, ceramics, and carbon. It compiles wavelength-dependent refractive indices and extinction coefficients from the literature. Each literature source is kept separate, together with its original conditions. One physics-based calculation chain turns these data into reflectivity, transmissivity, absorptivity, and emissivity for different incidence angles, slab thicknesses, and temperatures. Combined with the Air Mass Zero (AM0) solar spectrum, the properties give absorbed, reflected, and transmitted solar flux for concentrated sunlight. Equilibrium temperatures are given for both a theoretical lumped body and for a slab body, in which thermal conduction is considered. All data are limited to the solid state, up to a material-specific upper temperature limit. Currently, the database applies to extraterrestrial (AM0) sunlight only. A graphical App is also provided for exploring and visualizing the database.

papers.title: Pulsar Timing Correlations Induced by Stochastic Spin-2 Ultralight Dark Matter
papers.summary: Ultralight dark matter (ULDM) can generate time-dependent gravitational perturbations, providing a potential signal for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). In Galactic halos, the velocity dispersion of ULDM gives rise to finite spatial coherence, which influences the correlations between pulsar timing signals. In this work, we derive the timing-residual cross-correlations induced by rapid metric oscillations of spin-2 ULDM, allowing for general polarization statistics. Under equipartition among the five polarization modes, the intrinsic angular kernel contains monopole and quadrupole components and exhibits an angular profile closely resembling that of spin-1 ULDM, suggesting a potential degeneracy between the two ULDM candidates in PTA observations.

papers.title: Mono-Z Signatures of Vector Dark Matter Detection at Future Electron-Positron Colliders: FCC-ee and ILC
papers.summary: We investigate the mono-$Z$ signature of a vector dark matter (VDM) model at future electron-positron colliders. In this model, a stable vector boson, arising from an extended $U(1)$ gauge symmetry, serves as a viable DM candidate that interacts with the Standard Model (SM) through a Higgs portal. We perform a detailed cut-based analysis for the mono-$Z$ channel at the FCC-ee (with $\sqrt{s}=240$ and $365$ GeV) and the ILC (with $\sqrt{s}=1$ TeV), considering both leptonic and hadronic decays of the $Z$ boson. Signal significances are evaluated for benchmark points using fast event simulation with MadGraph5, PYTHIA8, and Delphes3. Our results demonstrate that future $e^+e^-$ colliders provide excellent sensitivity to Higgs-portal VDM, with the ILC's beam polarization offering an additional handle to suppress SM backgrounds. This study highlights the potential of lepton colliders in probing DM interactions.

papers.title: Soft momentum expansion about the Stokes topological limit of Bogoliubov coefficients
papers.summary: It is known that particle production in time-dependent cosmological backgrounds can be computed using the Stokes phenomena occurring in Bogoliubov transformations with an analytically continued time coordinate. We analytically compute the soft momentum expansion of the particle production amplitude about the Stokes topological limit that was recently discovered in this context. The computational technique relies on an exponentially improved asymptotic expansion that involves automorphisms in the space of functions defined partly by the angular step function intrinsic to the Stokes topological sectors. We combine this with special discrete symmetries tied to the time dependence of the dispersion relation $ω_k^2(z) = C(k) + A z^n$ for even $n$ to explicitly compute the leading momentum dependence of the amplitude which is nonperturbative in $A$. We also use this result to give a semi-analytic estimate of the number density of particles in this class of scenarios.

papers.title: SCOPE: A Physical Execution Latency-Guided Quantum Circuit Compilation Framework
papers.summary: Quantum computing requires compilers to translate algorithms represented in the quantum circuit model into unitary operations supported by physical devices. Limited coherence time makes physical execution latency an important compilation objective. Gate fusion can shorten pulses, but gate count and depth do not capture fused targets' control demands. Evaluating every candidate with quantum optimal control (QOC) would embed pulse optimization in structural search. We present Schmidt-guided Compilation for Optimized Pulse Execution (SCOPE), driven by an operator Schmidt time surrogate. The target's angular distance from product operators measures the required nonlocal change; dividing it by a coupling-limited evolution-rate bound gives a lower bound on exact implementation time. Trace-angle and waveform constraints complete block scores for critical-path evaluation during genetic search. Local QOC determines final pulse durations. Under a numerical nearest-neighbor control model, all 104 results across 13 instances from four application families have shorter QOC critical-path durations than an adapted efficient pulse generation framework with advanced synthesis for quantum circuits (EPOC). Using eight-run instance means, the equally weighted reduction is 42.50\%, with a geometric mean speedup of 2.00. In a shared six-qubit quantum Fourier transform (QFT) ablation, time-surrogate guidance reduces mean QOC duration by 22.21\% relative to gate-count guidance and 21.01\% relative to depth guidance, validating the surrogate's joint use in fitness evaluation and mutation-region selection.

papers.title: Variance-adaptive confidence regions for fixed-benchmark binomial mixtures, with application to LLM evaluation
papers.summary: We construct confidence intervals for linear functionals $θ(F_m)=\int h\,dF_m$ of the empirical law $F_m$ of success probabilities $p_1,\dots,p_m$, from independent counts $c_i\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n,p_i)$, as for a language model run $n$ times per problem. Coverage is at least $1-α$ for every $n$, $m$ and fixed $(p_i)$, simultaneously for all bounded $h$. The variance-adaptive (VA) region tests each candidate mixing law with the conditional variance of the tail counts it implies. This variance is linear in the law, so the region is a linear program, and cell envelopes keep it valid off-grid. Regions calibrated for iid sampling target a super-population law and are conservative for $θ(F_m)$. With all $n$ tail counts, fixed $n$, continuous $h$ and a grid refined as $m\to\infty$, the identification part of VA's width is first-order worst-case optimal, as for any localization with the same index set. Under a rule fixed before the main comparator runs, VA was narrower than a two-stage plug-in band at every $n$ (median width ratio 0.60 at $n=128$), but not than the asymptotic, pointwise AMARI interval at $n=128$; on real rollout pools it was wider than both pointwise and Bonferroni-adjusted AMARI at $n\le128$. For $P(p>0)$ and pass@$k$ with $k\gg n$ the data support only lower bounds.
papers.comment: 27 pages main text plus 57-page supplement. Code: https://github.com/YYKKCC-kevin/valoc

papers.title: Quantum-Assisted D-FACTS Scheduling for Moving Target Defense under Switching Limits
papers.summary: Moving target defense with distributed flexible alternating-current transmission system (D-FACTS) devices re- quires activation decisions as operating points change. Switching limits couple these decisions, but period-by-period rankings can overlook combinations needed to complete low-activation schedules. This paper proposes cross-period candidate sharing and schedule-completion evaluation to allocate limited physical checks in quantum-assisted D-FACTS scheduling. The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) generates activation candidates, while classical scheduling enforces operating and switching constraints. We also quantify model-based activation requirements and test detection through noisy nonlinear trials. A modified IEEE 118-bus study assesses recovery of reference activation and switching objectives within the evaluated set. Combining candidate sharing and schedule-completion evaluation improves final-budget recovery over period-by-period ranking in the primary operating window for every tested candidate generator. The results show that quantum and classical candidates yield identical recovery curves under combined checking, so the same allocation policy applies to either source.

papers.title: Hybrid Optimization-Generative Motion Planning for Multiagent Affine Formations
papers.summary: Formation maneuver control enables a multiagent system to cooperatively navigate through constrained environments in collective motion. While various formation controllers exist, they rely heavily on high-quality and dynamically feasible reference trajectories provided a priori, making formation motion planning (FMP) essential. To address the computational challenges for high-dimensional joint trajectories faced by conventional constrained optimization-based solutions, this paper introduces a hybrid optimization-generative framework with a focus on affine formations, which provide the necessary spatial flexibility. By formulating the planning task as a constrained Maximum-a-Posteriori estimation, we decouple multiagent objectives to leverage pre-trained single-agent diffusion priors for dynamic feasibility, obstacle avoidance, and smoothness. We then interleave the generative process with projected gradient descent (PGD) to strictly enforce affine geometric constraints with safety guarantees. Simulations demonstrate that our framework generates highly smooth, collision-free plans that are readily trackable by common distributed controllers and outperforms state-of-the-art planners in various metrics.

papers.title: Strategic Repayment and Latent Fragility in Financial Networks: Why Banks Withhold Payable Liquidity
papers.summary: A network in which every bank pays in full can nevertheless admit a self-fulfilling settlement freeze under the same balance-sheet fundamentals. Thus, observing full repayment does not establish the uniqueness or robustness of the payment equilibrium. We derive this result from a precautionary-liquidity choice: banks may delay otherwise feasible payments to insure an interim funding need, trading a positive settlement-discipline cost against the marginal value of retained cash. The optimal reserve is a critical quantile of future liquidity requirements, and the repayment rule nests Eisenberg-Noe maximal feasible clearing exactly. Counterparty underpayment both reduces current cash and raises desired reserves. We characterise network amplification and the conditions for coexistence, including a homogeneous two-bank GPD frontier in which interbank exposure and maximum funding pass-through enter through one dimensionless index. A two-date settlement accounting rule distinguishes payment timing from ultimate default. The main result concerns equilibrium coexistence; the conditional best-response adjustment diagnostic does not assign selection probabilities.

papers.title: Leveraging Binary Hashing for Scalable Index Assignment in Semantic Communications
papers.summary: Transmitting semantically structured embedding vectors over digital channels is costly in bit rate, while conven- tional vector quantization approaches face limitations in scalabil- ity, encoding complexity, and index assignment. This paper inves- tigates binary hashing techniques from the information retrieval literature as semantic indexing strategies for general-purpose networks. We study random Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) along with Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-, Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA)-, and ITQ (Iterative Quantization)- based variants in a semantic communication pipeline over a Binary Symmetric Channel. Embeddings are compressed into binary codes, reconstructed through Hamming retrieval from a shared table, and evaluated on downstream classification. Ex- periments on the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) and the Banking77 dataset show that data-dependent hashing improves upon random LSH, while ITQ refinement increases robustness to channel noise. Among the evaluated methods, CCA- ITQ achieves the best classification accuracy across the tested channel conditions. These results indicate that binary hashing is an efficient and scalable alternative to quantization-based embedding compression for semantic communications.

papers.title: ThinkWAM: Rethinking Latent Futures for Action Refinement
papers.summary: World-action models (WAMs) couple action generation with predictions of future states. An initial action chunk may be flawed. A future prediction that is not conditioned on the chunk may fail to reflect the changes that the proposed actions would induce in visual representations, limiting its usefulness for refinement before execution. We introduce ThinkWAM, a latent WAM that establishes bidirectional feedback before execution through a proposal-rethink-refine loop: the policy first proposes a complete action chunk, the proposal corrects multi-horizon future latents through a learned residual, and the corrected latents are injected into a second pass of the same action head, which generates the executable chunk. An affordance-guided observation-action memory and a near-fine, far-coarse multi-horizon prediction scheme, both motivated by predictive coding, support this loop, and all prediction stays in latent space. ThinkWAM achieves 98.70% success on LIBERO, 84.76% on LIBERO-Plus without OOD fine-tuning, 85.75%/65.85% on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean/Random, and 65.17% on RoboCasa24. ThinkWAM achieves 64.4% mean success across three real-world OOD conditions. The mean two-pass inference latency per action chunk is 153.48 ms on LIBERO, 164.61 ms on RoboTwin, and 101.2 ms on the Galaxea A1Z. Ablations show complementary gains from rethinking and affordance guidance. Diagnostics indicate that proposal-conditioned corrections change both predicted futures and action trajectories, showing that the corrected future representations improve the final action.
papers.comment: 21 pages, including references and appendix. Project page: https://thinkwam-project.github.io/

papers.title: Continuous Phase-Coherent Readout of a Magneto-Mechanical Resonator Using a Phase-Locked Loop
papers.summary: Magneto-mechanical resonators are wireless sensors that encode a measurand in their natural frequency. Existing systems estimate this frequency from repeated cycles of excitation and ring-down, which limits the precision and bandwidth range. Here, we introduce a continuous, phase-coherent readout based on a phase-locked loop. In a benchtop setup, one record stayed within 4 % of the precision-bandwidth limit over more than three decades of bandwidth, while conventional readouts remained about a factor of 4 above it.
papers.comment: 2 pages, 2 figures, Sensor and Measurement Science International Conference (SMSI) 2027 conference

papers.title: Phenomenology of neutrino mass ordering synergies in reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric neutrino experiments, and the role of the detector response
papers.summary: The neutrino mass ordering is one of the main open questions of neutrino physics, addressed by reactor, accelerator, and atmospheric experiments and by their combination. When the data are fitted under the wrong ordering, each experiment returns its own value of $Δm^2_{31}$, its wrong-ordering solution. We show that this solution is a weighted average of the values preferred by the individual bins of the measured event spectra, in reconstructed energy and, for atmospheric neutrinos, also zenith angle, with weights set by their statistical precision. Both the values and the weights depend on the detector response. In the plane of $Δm^2_{31}$ fitted under the two orderings, the solutions lie on lines of slope close to $-1$, so that each experiment is described by one intercept. The weighted bin average extends the mass ordering sum rule to any oscillation experiment, including atmospheric neutrinos in Earth matter. It recovers the known closed forms for short-baseline reactors and for accelerators in vacuum, and for JUNO it equals a closed form evaluated at one effective energy, which depends on the energy resolution. Above the MSW resonance the frequency of atmospheric $ν_μ$ disappearance becomes nearly independent of $δ_{CP}$, and the $ν_μ$ disappearance solution moves mainly with $θ_{23}$. The atmospheric intercept depends on the energy and direction resolutions, the energy window, and the event classes, and differs between detectors. The synergy of two experiments is determined by the separation of their intercepts relative to their precisions on $|Δm^2_{31}|$. With JUNO, this separation depends strongly on $δ_{CP}$ for an accelerator and is nearly independent of $δ_{CP}$ and $θ_{23}$ for IceCube DeepCore using all channels.
papers.comment: 46 pages, 14 figures, 2 tables. Code available at https://github.com/vanessacerrone/nmo-synergies

papers.title: Heteroscedastic Gaussian Process Q-learning for Sample Efficient Experimentation
papers.summary: Self-driving laboratories must learn to control a process from tens to hundreds of expensive experiments, too few for deep reinforcement learning (RL). We learn the Q-function directly with a Gaussian process (GP), which avoids learning the dynamics, and show that the GP posterior supplies the learning rate of Q-learning. If each Bellman target is treated as a noisy measurement of the Q-function, the learning rate that minimises the mean squared error is the Kalman gain, and applying it to every observed transition is equivalent to GP regression. Heteroscedastic Gaussian Process Q-learning (HGPQ) sets the noise variance of each target with a heteroscedastic GP, which learns how unreliable the targets are across the states and inputs. Targets from noisy operating conditions, or from regions where the value function has large gradients, then move the estimate less than targets from low-noise regions, so HGPQ learns quickly where the data are reliable without being misled where they are not. For kernel value iteration with per-target variances that are assigned when a target is collected, we prove a high-probability bound on the error of the value estimate, uniform over the explored region. Pooled over five simulated benchmarks, which include a chemical reactor and a bioprocess, HGPQ approaches the best return found by any method in fewer episodes than GP, kernel and deep RL baselines.

papers.title: Neurosymbolic Synthesis of Contraction Metrics with Certified Verification
papers.summary: We study counterexample-guided synthesis of contraction metrics for continuous-time autonomous systems on compact domains. A learner proposes a metric; a sound verifier certifies its matrix inequality or returns diagnostic points for retraining. The neural extension pairs a learned metric factor with symbolic contraction conditions and rigorous numerical verification; main ablations use polynomial features. We give computable polynomial bounds in arbitrary dimension and outward-rounded verification for polynomial, trigonometric, and neural representations. Loop soundness is separated from conditional finite-grid termination under idealized feasibility assumptions. We analyze why scaling and fixed-margin training can leave valid metrics uncertified. The scaling construction requires a scale-closed family, which the experimental fixed-floor class generally lacks. Verified slack improves the contraction rate and quantifies model-error tolerances using certified residual and Jacobian bounds. Finite-distance conclusions require connecting paths whose flows stay in the verified region. Experiments include controlled ablations, three-dimensional verification, and transfer from a fitted surrogate with known-truth residual certification. A physical swing-model study compares neural learning objectives with shared verification and invariant energy regions. Verified constant metrics certify the polynomial benchmark and smallest swing-model domain; neither result requires neural state dependence. Exploratory refinement certifies additional frozen candidates at a larger verification budget. In matched polynomial operating-grid experiments, trace normalization and margin coupling did not demonstrate a certification-count advantage within the tested budgets. These choices address specific failure mechanisms without guaranteeing optimizer convergence or general empirical superiority.
papers.comment: 30 pages, 10 figures. Code and verified reproduction: https://github.com/vmpreciado/NeuroSymbolic/releases/tag/v1.2.2

papers.title: Noise and quasi-periodic oscillations in black hole accretion flows
papers.summary: Temporal fluctuations of the viscosity parameter at different radii in an accretion flow are known to give rise to variability in the accretion rate onto the black hole. The power spectrum of accretion-rate fluctuations is expected to exhibit a broad-band power-law dependence on frequency (e.g., flicker noise). We show that viscosity fluctuations can also generate quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the power spectrum. In our model, QPOs are caused by reflection of accretion-rate fluctuations at the outer radius of the accretion flow and arise near the low-frequency break of the power spectrum, which corresponds to the inverse viscous timescale at the outer radius. These QPOs occur in geometrically thick advection-dominated accretion flows but are absent in geometrically thin cooling-dominated flows.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics

papers.title: All-sky spectroscopic survey of bright δ Scuti stars from TESS Projected rotational velocities and pulsation characteristics
papers.summary: Context. The second most numerous class of pulsating stars -- $δ$ Scuti ($δ$ Sct) -- lack a homogeneous, large-scale spectroscopic sample in the Kepler and TESS era, limiting our understanding of how rotation shapes stellar pulsations. Aims. We analyse projected rotational velocities ($v \sin i$) from high-resolution spectroscopy alongside 2-minute TESS photometry to establish empirical links between stellar rotation and pulsation parameters. Methods. Combining observations from three high-resolution échelle spectrographs with two spectral libraries, we assemble an all-sky sample of 262 $δ$ Sct stars ($R = 25\,000$ to $115\,000$). We derive $v \sin i$ via three independent methods and extract pulsation frequencies and amplitudes from TESS light curves. Results. The $v \sin i$ distribution is unimodal, with a mean of $120.3\text{ km s}^{-1}$ and peak probability at $113.8\text{ km s}^{-1}$. Minimum ($ν_{\rm min}$), dominant ($ν_{\rm dom}$), amplitude-weighted ($ν_{\rm AW}$), and power-weighted ($ν_{\rm PW}$) frequencies decrease with $v \sin i / v_{\rm crit}$, whereas maximum frequency ($ν_{\rm max}$) does not. Fast rotators show a narrower range of photometric and pulsation amplitudes than slow rotators, and their lower mean stellar density ($\barρ$) cannot fully explain the frequency decrease. Calibrating Gaia's $v_{\rm broad}$ against our measurements removes its systematic offset, enabling use across larger $δ$ Sct samples. Multi-spectrum comparisons reveal method discrepancies mainly for fast rotators ($v \sin i > 200\text{ km s}^{-1}$) and inter-spectrograph offsets up to $20\text{ km s}^{-1}$. Conclusions. We present the largest homogeneous high-resolution $v \sin i$ sample for bright $δ$ Sct stars in the TESS era, showing that $v \sin i$ measurements in pulsating stars require careful treatment across instruments and velocity regimes.

papers.title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
papers.summary: We present a transferable Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) model for bismuth with explicit spin-orbit coupling that enables exploration of the structural degrees of freedom governing topological properties with minimal computational resources. We have used our DFTB model to run high-throughput calculations at a scale that would be significantly more expensive with standard Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) to determine a strain-buckling map of electronic and topological properties for bismuthene, where we identify regions of band gap closure and band inversion as a function of structural parameters. We show that our approach yields an accurate band structure for the rhombohedral phase, where small band gaps exist at or near time-reversal-invariant momentum (TRIM) points. We then demonstrate the transferability of our model to bismuth properties not included in our training data through determination of the rhombohedral phase phonon density of states and energetic ordering of additional bismuth solid phases. Finally, we have validated our topological predictions through comparison to DFT results for the optimized bilayer geometries, a band inversion order parameter, and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant as a function of monolayer unit cell length. Our efforts establish DFTB as a rigorous approach for topological characterization while yielding approximately three orders of magnitude increase in computational efficiency relative to DFT. Our model can thus serve as a computational tool for topological materials discovery by enabling large-scale computational screening to address the potentially complex relationship between physical-chemical properties and the resulting topological classification.

papers.title: Slower but Faster: When Self-Organized Traffic Flows Beat Traffic Signal Control
papers.summary: Urban traffic flow networks are complex adaptive systems, whose variability challenges centralized, top-down control. We study decentralized alternatives in which order emerges from local interactions, comparing the network-wide performance of roundabouts in SUMO against fixed-time and actuated control as well as self-organizing signals on a 4$\times$4 grid and a rewired, irregular variant of it, across demand levels and periodic surge amplitudes. In our computer simulations of the regular grid, converting the single most central intersection already lowers delays by 2 to 3\% relative to actuated control; each additional conversion lowers them further, and full conversion outperforms every signalized alternative under all conditions studied. In the irregular traffic flow network with full conversion of all intersections into roundabouts, this holds only up to a critical load, where traffic flow breaks down sharply, when the time-averaged demand reaches about 3.1 times the base load. Beyond that point, the self-organizing traffic signals show the lowest delay of any network-wide strategy and is nearly insensitive to surges. Interestingly, roundabouts are favorable solutions even at lower speed limits: in the regular grid, compared to the mean speed under actuated control at a speed limit of 50\,km/h, roundabouts match that speed at a speed limit of about 40\,km/h. Compared to traffic signal control, this establishes a slower-is-faster effect. Furthermore, travel times in self-organized traffic flows are more predictable than in networks with conventional signals.

papers.title: A boson representation of the electronic structure calculation based on the quantum Krylov subspace algorithm
papers.summary: Quantum calculations are expected to broaden the range of strongly correlated phenomena in solids accessible to first-principles calculations. The quantum Krylov diagonalization method, or in a broader sense, the quantum subspace expansion method (QSE) offers an advantage over other variational methods in terms of numerical stability. In this work, we propose a boson representation of electronic systems with the aim of reducing QSE quantum circuit depth, where electron-hole pair bosons serve as the fundamental degrees of freedom. We benchmark the boson representation in comparison with a corresponding fermionic QSE and CCSD for an equidistant and a dimerized configuration of a periodic hydrogen chain \ce{(H2)_n}. Despite the drastic approximation we reveal the boson QSE scheme provides practically useful accuracy in the ground state energy. Our results support its applicability to realistic quasi-two- and three-dimensional electronic systems.

papers.title: What kind of quantum advantage is this?
papers.summary: Quantum advantage encompasses fundamentally different claims, from resource reductions to exponential separations in sample complexity.
