Without compensation, the risk of losing creators and their training data constrains the platform to set the price of creators' content to preserve their demand. This constraint also prevents further AI displacement as AI improves, with the platform raising AI prices while keeping creators' prices and demand unchanged to prevent exit. Compensation increases creators' payoffs and total surplus but reduces consumer surplus. Our findings highlight how compensation policies for training data can shape creators' economic roles in a future with more capable generative AI.
papers.comment: 53 pages, 6 figures. Previously circulated under the title "Platform Design When Creators Train Their AI Substitutes"

papers.title: Automated Left Ventricle Strain Analysis from DENSE MRI
papers.summary: Background: Quantifying myocardial strains from Displacement ENcoding with Stimulated Echoes (DENSE) MRI provides insight into left ventricular performance, but current data processing pipelines remain limited in automation, robustness, and full left ventricle coverage. Methods: We present a fully automated framework for voxel-wise displacement and strain analysis of the left ventricle from DENSE MRI. Our method integrates a multi-channel nnU-Net model trained on both magnitude and phase images for segmentation, an automated phase unwrapping approach, an adaptation of the regularized spatiotemporal least squares (RSTLS) formulation for displacement computation, and strain calculations based on radial basis function interpolation. The proposed framework enables the estimation of displacements and strains across the left ventricle from a full stack of short-axis images. Results: Validation using a computational phantom shows the framework's overall resilience to data noise. Following computational phantom evaluation, the proposed framework is applied to analyze DENSE MRI short-axis slices acquired in forty-seven (N=47) healthy volunteers and covering the full left ventricle. Circumferential, longitudinal, and radial strains are presented throughout the cardiac cycle and at peak systole, showcasing the performance of the proposed framework. Results show that circumferential and longitudinal strains are computed accurately. However, challenges persist when estimating radial strain, especially in the subendocardial layer. A group-wise strain comparison is also performed based on volunteers' sex and age showing a significant effect of sex on circumferential and longitudinal strains. Conclusions: Overall, the proposed framework provides an automated and modular pipeline to compute displacements and strains from DENSE MR images that can be scaled and generalized toward clinical applications.

papers.title: Study on net-proton number fluctuations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{\textit{s}_{\text{NN}}}$ = 7.7-27 GeV with the SMASH model
papers.summary: Higher-order cumulants ($C_n$) of the event-by-event net-proton number ($ΔN_{\mathrm{p}} = N_{\mathrm{p}} - N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}$) distributions are sensitive observables in the search for the QCD critical point. A reliable quantitative baseline for non-critical effects is essential for interpreting these observables. We calculate $C_2/\langle N_{\mathrm{p}} + N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}\rangle$, $C_3/C_1$, and $C_4/C_2$ in Au+Au collisions at collision energies $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 7.7$-$27$ GeV with the SMASH hadronic transport model. The collision-centrality, rapidity-window, and collision-energy dependences are reported. The cumulant ratios are predicted below the independent-Poisson baseline, with the suppression increasing toward more central collisions and larger rapidity windows. In 70-80% collisions, SMASH calculations lie above the STAR measurements for all three ratios, whereas in 0-5% collisions, the STAR $C_4/C_2$ value at 19.6 GeV lies below the SMASH reference with a pull of approximately $-2.7$. These results provide an independent non-critical hadronic baseline for assessing the model dependence of the observed data-model discrepancies.

papers.title: From the possible to the optimal: differentiable optimization of gene regulatory networks
papers.summary: Understanding the space of ``the actual and the possible'' regulatory architectures capable of realizing biological functions is one of the major challenges in biology. Optimization-based approaches can rationalize regulatory mechanisms from functional objectives and constraints, but their computational cost has limited them to finding individual solutions. Here, we introduce \texttt{jaxgrn}, a framework that combines differentiable programming with stochastic simulations of gene regulatory networks (GRNs) to optimize thousands of networks end-to-end on GPUs. Using morphogen-driven embryonic patterning as a case study, we optimize networks for domain formation and positional information, while varying constraints on input noise, boundary precision and scaling with system size. While recovering known archetypes for scaling, we find that varying the constraints organizes optimal solutions into qualitatively distinct regimes. When optimizing domain formation, we observe phenotypic convergence across a continuum of regulatory architectures, ranging from input-driven to feedback-driven networks. When optimizing positional information, solutions are initially phenotypically diverse despite moderate variation in regulatory architecture; imposing scaling drives both phenotypic and regulatory convergence of the optimized networks onto a few recurring regulatory architectures. Our systematic approach opens the door for variational systems biology in which changing functional constraints reshape the landscape of possible phenotypes and regulatory architectures.

papers.title: Log-optimal portfolios for market models with regime switching
papers.summary: This paper considers market models under regime switching mechanism with $D$ states, and analyses the log-optimal portfolio. It is the portfolio, with finite expected utility, that maximizes the logarithmic utility from terminal wealth. We consider a family $\mathbb{X}=(X^{(i)})_{i=1,...,D}$, of $D$-semimartingale models, among which our agent can switch to-and-from following a switching regime modelled by a continuous-time Markov Chain $α=(α_t)_{t\geq 0}$ with $α_0=1$. Then we define a general switching model $\widehat{X}$ that covers the existing cases, and study the impact of the stochasticity of the regime switching and its intrinsic risks on the optimal portfolio in many aspects. On the one hand, we single out the necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(\mathbb{X},α)$, which guarantee the existence of the optimal portfolio for $\widehat{X}$. On the other hand, we quantify the factors that fully affect and determine the increment in maximum expected logarithmic utility from terminal wealth for both models $\widehat{X}$ and $X^{(1)}$.

papers.title: Nuclear Mott transition with neural quantum states
papers.summary: Bound clusters can dissolve in nuclear matter due to Pauli blocking, a phenomenon known as the Mott transition that is a key determinant of the nuclear abundances in heavy-ion collisions. Microscopic descriptions of this behavior require solving the in-medium Schrödinger equation. However, this remains a major computational challenge because the nuclear medium breaks Galilean invariance and couples angular-momentum channels at finite center-of-mass momentum. The emergence of weakly bound states near dissociation further places stringent demands on conventional methods. Here, we address these challenges by introducing MottNet, a momentum-space neural quantum state framework based on self-attention that directly solves the $A$-body in-medium Schrödinger equation. Benchmarked against exact diagonalization of the in-medium deuteron, MottNet reveals substantially weaker Mott suppression for $α$ particles in hot and dense nuclear matter than do conventional calculations based on combined approximations. At high baryon densities, the predicted $α$-particle abundance is enhanced by orders of magnitude, even after continuum-edge subtraction. This finding offers a microscopic explanation for the unexpectedly large $α$-particle fraction inferred from a combined analysis of FOPI heavy-ion collision data and transport model calculations.

papers.title: Who Observes Whom: Network Rationalizability and Its Complexity
papers.summary: Nash equilibrium and rationalizability sit at opposite informational extremes: the former presumes that each player knows all opponents' strategies, the latter that players reason from common knowledge of rationality alone. When visibility is partial and asymmetric, we study the solution concepts induced by a directed \emph{observation network} $G$ in which an edge $i\to j$ means that $i$ observes $j$'s strategy. A set of profiles is \emph{self-sustaining} if every profile in it can be justified, for every player, by conjectures from the same set that agree with everything the player observes. We consider \emph{point} conjectures (single profiles) and \emph{belief} conjectures (distributions over profiles). Both range from Nash equilibrium on the complete network to point- and correlated rationalizability on the empty network, and shrink monotonically as links are added. Network topology governs both behavior and complexity. A predicted profile can be found in polynomial time on the empty network, whereas a single link makes search $\mathsf{PPAD}$-hard: under one-sided two-player monitoring, the observed player's strategies are exactly her Nash equilibrium strategies. On hierarchical networks (transitive tournaments), membership reduces recursively to smaller games and admits polynomial-size certificates, placing verification in $\exists\mathbb{R}$, and in $\mathsf{P}$ for two players. On the directed three-cycle, however, iterated elimination may never terminate under either variant, and under point conjectures interior predictions may admit only infinite witness sets, a pathology that belief conjectures avoid in the same game. Finally, when only realized pure actions are observed, the solution set is guaranteed to be non-empty exactly when the network has no edges, and is computable in time $O(n|A|^2)$.

papers.title: High-Dimensional Approximate Factor Models with Score-Driven Dynamics: Estimation and Inference
papers.summary: We propose a factor model for high-dimensional time series where the dynamics of the latent factors is generated by a multivariate score-driven model, thus allowing to model nonlinearities and heavy tails in both the conditional mean and the conditional variance. Estimation is in two steps: first the factors are extracted via Principal Components and then the parameters of the score-driven model are estimated via Quasi Maximum Likelihood based on the estimated factors. Since factors are not identified, we first establish set-consistency and asymptotic normality for the estimated parameters governing their dynamics, as both the number of time series and the sample size diverge to infinity. Then, we construct valid asymptotic prediction intervals, which do not depend on the chosen identifying constraints for the factors. Numerical results confirm the goodness of our estimator.

papers.title: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data
papers.summary: Real-world portfolio management requires converting noisy market observations into coordinated, simultaneous allocations across multiple assets under shared capital constraints. Advances in forecasting models and alpha discovery help identify opportunities. However, traditional pipelines often decouple signal forecasting from portfolio construction, potentially misaligning learning with allocation and execution objectives. We present AllocFlow, an end-to-end flow-matching framework that directly generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories. To capture dependencies among portfolio positions, AllocFlow employs a cross-asset flow Transformer conditioned on temporal market representations to generate continuous, signed position weights across all instruments jointly. To address the sample inefficiency and instability of learning continuous allocation policies from scratch, we establish a two-stage training scheme: strategy-supervised imitation shapes a structured distribution of candidate portfolios, followed by group-relative reinforcement learning (RL) that refines joint decisions using portfolio-level financial rewards and a frozen policy reference. On hourly cryptocurrency perpetual futures, RL refinement raises the annualized net return of the imitation policy from $27.79\%$ to $51.38\%$ and its Calmar ratio from $0.955$ to $4.043$, surpassing the teacher strategy on every metric, and AllocFlow reaches a Calmar ratio of $4.90$ on six further months of unseen 2026 data without retraining.

papers.title: Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Networks with Nested Clustered Optimization for Multi-Asset Portfolios
papers.summary: Nested Clustered Optimization (NCO) insulates asset allocation from Markowitz covariance ill-conditioning. However, classical tree clustering relies on static pairwise Pearson correlation, failing to capture time-varying, asymmetric downside risk contagion across multi-asset markets. We propose a unified deep graph machine learning architecture: Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Networks with Nested Clustered Optimization (ST-GAT-NCO) for multi-asset tactical allocation. The framework extracts temporal momentum and downside risk dynamics via causal dilated 1D-convolutions, then deploys a multi-head Graph Attention Network (GAT) over dynamic market topologies to learn latent spatial node representations. These learned embeddings define an angular metric distance space that guides two-stage downside NCO optimization under institutional constraints and turnover smoothing. Evaluated over a 73-month non-anticipative walk-forward out-of-sample window (January 2020 to January 2026) across 13 global asset classes net of 10 bps transaction costs, ST-GAT-NCO achieves a 5.32% CAGR and 37.06% cumulative net return, delivering an excess Sharpe ratio of 0.30 and a Sortino ratio of 0.48. This substantially outperforms classical Minimum Variance (3.68% CAGR, 0.08 Sharpe), Hierarchical Risk Parity (2.65% CAGR), and Plain Symmetric NCO (4.11% CAGR, 0.15 Sharpe), while restricting maximum drawdown to -13.07% (versus -19.44% for Equal-Weight and -16.36% for Downside NCO) under a controlled one-way turnover of 15.31%/month. Regime analysis confirms active capital preservation across the 2020 COVID-19 crash, 2022 monetary tightening, and 2023-2026 disinflation rallies.
papers.comment: 10 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Replication package and dataset available at https://github.com/obo-cloud/multiasset-stgat-nco

papers.title: An Exploration of Physical and Chemical Representation in Coarse-Grained, Machine-Learned Protein Models
papers.summary: Machine-learned coarse-graining has emerged as a reliable framework for building protein models that accurately and efficiently sample their relevant conformational landscape. Existing studies assume a predefined map from full- to coarse-grained resolution. However, the choice of map strongly affects the quality of the models. Here, we study the dependence of system-specific machine-learned coarse-grained (MLCG) models across 7 mapping choices, spanning different resolutions and embedding types for coarse-grained beads. We show that resolution and chemical diversity do not always correlate with accuracy, and that accurate protein-specific models can be generated using minimal chemical diversity if the latent space representation of the system has high enough dimensionality.

papers.title: Toward an Admissibility Theory of Aharonov--Bohm Arbitrage
papers.summary: This note develops a provisional admissibility framework for Aharonov-Bohm type arbitrage. Starting from a categorical filtration $F:\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mic}}^{\mathrm{op}}\to \mathsf{Prob}$ and its distortion on microscopic histories, we ask when a favorable closed microscopic loop can be realized as an executable relative ordinal arbitrage over an open macro-time interval. The history endofunctor $\mathsf{Hist}$ retains the staged decomposition of economic activities, while the twisted-arrow category $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathsf{Hist}(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mic}}))$ represents a microscopic loop as an arrow between distinct histories. An observable clock $Π: \mathsf{Econ} \to \mathcal T_{\mathrm{mac}}$ and a microscopic realization functor $J: \mathsf{Hist}(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mac}}) \to \operatorname{Tw}(\mathsf{Hist}(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mic}}))$ connect economic histories with their microscopic geometry. Executability is treated separately through configuration histories, capacity constraints, observations, and policies. This yields pathwise and almost-sure notions of execution. A finite foreign-exchange model illustrates stochastic execution, capacity failure, terminal settlement, and comparison with a benchmark strategy. A parameterized finite filtration is constructed whose nontrivial statewise distortion agrees exactly with the relative FX settlement multiplier. Hence the resulting filtration--policy model satisfies the bridge $V_*(π^q)=dF(γ)V_*(π^p),$ and, under order compatibility, realizes relative ordinal arbitrage. The remaining problem is to identify the filtration parameters from independent market primitives and to study stability under refinement.

papers.title: Indication of demographic and epidemiological data on early-stage risks and long-term epidemic burden
papers.summary: This study investigates the relationship between age-specific cumulative infection burden and the probability of triggering a major outbreak in heterogeneous populations. We develop two modeling frameworks that incorporate empirical age-stratified contact matrices: a deterministic framework for deriving the final size relation and a stochastic framework based on a Continuous-time Markov chain epidemic model, for which a multi-type branching-process approximation is used to characterize early-stage outbreak risk. The framework is illustrated using empirical social contact data from Guangzhou, Foshan, and Zhuhai, China, under two disease-motivated scenarios representing COVID-19 and hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD). The illustrative analyses indicate that the relationship between cumulative infection burden and early-stage outbreak risk depends on both epidemiological characteristics and population contact patterns. In particular, age groups with the highest final attack rates do not necessarily have the highest probability of triggering a major outbreak. These findings highlight the complementary nature of the two measures and the value of considering both when assessing age-specific epidemic risks in practice.

papers.title: NoLBERT-Calls: Reading Earnings Calls Without Hindsight
papers.summary: Language models are now a standard tool for measuring what managers say on earnings calls, but the encoders behind these measures were usually pretrained on text from the same years a backtest covers. Holding out a test period does not remove that hindsight, because it sits in the features. We adapt NoLBERT, an encoder pretrained only on text published between 1976 and 1995, to earnings calls without letting it read anything dated after 31 December 2023. The calls supply the training signal themselves: every analyst question is followed by management's answer, and the model learns to pick that answer out from the other answers of the same call. We test on every US call from January 2025 to October 2026 (20,323 calls, 254,575 questions) and make every modeling choice on calls from 2024. The adapted model, NoLBERT-Calls-2023, ranks the true answer first for 78.0% of questions (95% interval 77.8-78.2; chance 8.0%), against 26.3% before adaptation. It is 1.0 point ahead of a call-adapted ChronoBERT, 3.4 points ahead of a call-adapted FinBERT, and 18.7 and 19.8 points ahead of the best off-the-shelf retriever and BM25. A year-by-year test over 2013-2026 finds no look-ahead premium: relative to a model adapted only through 2012, the released model does no better on the years it was trained on than on years it never saw. The price of the cutoff is compute: under one shared 150-minute recipe NoLBERT adapts least well of four encoders, and its lead comes from a longer, staged adaptation of about 13 GPU-hours.

papers.title: Reasoning in the loop: antibody lead optimization by probing mechanism and measurement
papers.summary: Lab-in-the-loop systems, in which a model proposes molecules, automated assays measure their properties and the results retrain the model, are a popular approach to antibody lead optimization. These systems optimize for a specification defined with metrics computed from instrument signals, so their success depends on how well those metrics serve as proxies for the properties a drug candidate needs. When a metric is a poor proxy, neither a better model nor more data will fix it, and identifying the problem usually requires expert review. We report two campaigns run on BigHat Biosciences' Milliner platform, one on an anti-albumin nanobody (VHH) and one on an anti-mesothelin single-chain variable fragment (scFv), in which a research team and a general-purpose AI agent, Claude, brought scientific reasoning into the loop. Over seven rounds and about 1,010 design variants we built libraries from antibody lineage, structure and biophysics, and found from the raw curves that on each scaffold one thermal metric did not measure what its name implied. The libraries were built as controlled comparisons, so the results also show what each mutation contributes to each property. We fit a physical model of the curves, used it to choose metrics suited to each scaffold, and changed the experimental protocol, varying protein concentration and heating rate, to test the model against pre-registered predictions. Both leads improve on their parents in affinity, thermal stability and aggregation while improving or maintaining yield and purity.

papers.title: PIRanNN: Random-Feature Pricing and Calibration under Jump-Diffusion and Stochastic-Volatility Models
papers.summary: We study a random-feature method for pricing and calibrating European options under jump-diffusion (Merton, Kou) and stochastic-volatility (Heston, SABR) models. The network has one hidden layer with a probit activation and fixed random inner weights, so fitting it to the pricing equation, the payoff and the boundary conditions is a single regularised least-squares problem, with no iterative training. For Merton and Kou the jump integral of each feature is explicit, so no quadrature is needed. One factorisation of the least-squares matrix gives the price at every state and time, its Greeks, and the exact derivatives of the prices with respect to the model parameters for gradient-based calibration. For the jump models, subtracting the Black-Scholes price removes the payoff kink and reduces the pricing error by about two orders of magnitude. The method is then about as accurate as a standard Crank-Nicolson finite-difference scheme at the same run time, although a finite-difference scheme that also subtracts the Black-Scholes price is about two orders of magnitude more accurate still. On the test problems of a recent physics-informed neural network study, the method matches that network's accuracy in seconds instead of about half an hour. The calibration experiments show that a solver can fit the quotes and still return wrong parameters when its pricing error is not small compared with the effect of the parameters on the prices: without the subtraction the solver misses the jump parameters by up to 50%, and with it they are recovered to within 3%. For Heston and SABR, used as an applicability study with boundary conditions that need no reference prices, pricing errors are about one percent and the calibrated parameters are within about 15% of the true values.

papers.title: Charm quark energy loss fluctuations in clumpy color string medium
papers.summary: We simulate charm quark propagation through an ensemble of color flux tubes formed between receding color charges in proton-proton collisions. Under the assumption of sharp string boundaries and a localized nature of the overlap regions, high flux tube densities lead to the formation of string clusters. We convert the local energy density of the superposed color field into an effective temperature of an ideal gluon gas and study the dependence of charm energy loss on its spatial inhomogeneities. By comparing different energy-density extraction prescriptions, we show that both elastic and inelastic momentum damping mechanisms are sensitive to the medium properties. However, the collisional channel is an order of magnitude smaller in absolute terms (up to $\sim0.15$~GeV) compared to the radiative loss (up to $\sim1.5$~GeV). Overall, the results demonstrate that the spatial overlap of individual strings generates a complex local energy density pattern, which predominantly governs the medium-induced quenching of charm quarks.
papers.comment: 16 pages, 9 figures, submitted to International Journal of Modern Physics E

papers.title: Fate of chiral and $U(1)_A$ symmetries in hot QCD matter under background magnetic fields
papers.summary: We summarize our recent lattice QCD study of chiral and singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking in background magnetic fields. The magnetic field explicitly reduces the non-singlet flavor symmetry through the unequal light-quark electric charges. We therefore study two neutral-channel susceptibility differences: $χ_{π^0}-χ_σ$ for chiral symmetry breaking and $χ_{π^0}-χ_{δ^0}$ for singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking. The calculation uses fixed-scale $(2+1)$-flavor HISQ ensembles with $m_l=m_s^{\mathrm{phys}}/10$, corresponding to a zero-field pion mass of $M_π\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$. Magnetic fields enhance both susceptibility differences at low temperatures. Near the crossover, sufficiently strong fields instead suppress both differences. The suppression sets in at larger magnetic fields and is milder for the singlet-axial susceptibility difference than for the neutral chiral susceptibility difference.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures; Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on QCD in Extreme Conditions (xQCD 2026), 14-17 July 2026, Busan, Korea

papers.title: Cross-species digital xenocortication model delineates molecular correlates of human brain connectome
papers.summary: Cross-species digital xenocortication (CSDX) model based on pairing of a human brain structure with one or more mouse brain structures was constructed and implemented to dissect the molecular correlates of the human brain connectome. Design of the CSDX model is based on the assumption that a human brain region and its named mouse counterpart occupy corresponding positions in an evolutionary conserved mammalian brain connectome plan, so that a projection strength measured between two mouse structures is informative about the relation between the two human structures paired with them. In the CSDX model, gene expression for the node was measured in the human brain, while connection strength between two nodes was measured in the mouse brain. CSDX models of different parcellations were employed to explore the potential regulatory associations of brain connectome patterns and constituents of protein-protein interaction (PPI) cascades of hybrid assembly pathways of endogenous multiprotein complexes. Metrics of continuous engagement of the PPI cascade nucleated protein dimers of CORUM multiprotein complexes have been identified as statistical components of the multivariate transcriptome-connectome associations. It accounts for additional connectome associated variations beyond the five measured axes in the 82 nodes CSDX model. Comparisons of the seven arm models of transcriptome-connectome associations demonstrate that the mouse derived model generally fits the mouse brain connectome better, while the human derived model assigns a significantly larger fraction of its transcriptome-connectome association to unique rather than net shared contributions. This study nominates elite panels of top scoring candidate protein dimers and CORUM multiprotein complexes for follow up mechanistic studies of their potential roles in structural functional features governing mammalian brain connectome.

papers.title: Analysis choices can produce apparent rich-club differences: an Alzheimer's disease EEG case study
papers.summary: The weighted rich-club coefficient tests whether a network's most strongly connected nodes are preferentially interconnected. Its interpretation depends on two often-implicit choices that are easy to overlook: how the randomised comparison networks are constructed, and whether the hubs are re-identified in each comparison network or held fixed at those of the observed network. When hubs are defined by connection strength, these choices change what the coefficient actually tests. We examined how these choices affect inference using resting-state EEG from 20 people with Alzheimer's disease and 20 controls. Holding the data fixed, we compared four analysis pipelines, crossing two ways of building the comparison networks with the two hub choices, and ran a calibration study in which the same pipelines were applied to data constructed to contain no preferential hub coupling. An apparent eyes-open group difference in rich-club organisation appeared under only one of the four pipelines, the one combining a global weight reshuffle with re-identified hubs, and was absent under the other three. More tellingly, that same pipeline reported a group difference in 40% of cases where none was present, almost always higher in the Alzheimer's disease group, while the other three stayed near the expected 5%. This shows that the same data can support or dissolve an apparent rich-club difference depending on choices that are rarely reported. No single choice is universally correct, but reporting which were made, and why they fit the question being asked, is essential to interpreting the result.
papers.comment: Submitted version (before peer review) of a Short Communication published in Journal of Neuroscience Methods; to be replaced by the accepted manuscript. 21 pages, 1 figure, 1 table, supplementary material appended

papers.title: Wobbling Motion in the Many-Nucleon System
papers.summary: The purpose of this Perspective is not to present a new progress but to shed light on another stream of the study of the nuclear wobbling motion from a viewpoint of the many-body theory under an external field. Special attention is paid to the moments of inertia, which are microscopically calculated as a response of the full $A$-body system to rapid rotations described by the cranked RPA formalism. They depend on the rotation frequency, and it is shown that approach of two moments of inertia leads to the instability of rotating triaxial mean fields.
papers.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, Frontiers in Physics, published
papers.journal: Matsuzaki M (2026) Wobbling motion in the many-nucleon system. Front. Phys. 14:1965157

papers.title: State-space symmetry in Boolean network ensembles
papers.summary: Studies of evolving Boolean network systems have found that Boolean functions cluster into equivalence classes with a characteristic frequency distribution - a pattern governed by the Zyklenzeiger symmetry group - but the dynamical origin of this symmetry has remained unexplained. Here we show that it is a consequence of a fundamental symmetry of Boolean network dynamics itself. A Boolean network consists of nodes that update according to Boolean functions of their regulatory inputs; its global dynamics is encoded in a state-space network. We identify the dynamical symmetry group of ensembles of Boolean networks that average over random interaction topologies: for networks with $N$ nodes, it is the $N$-dimensional hyperoctahedral group, generated by node-flips and node-label permutations. These transformations are admissible for every Boolean network regardless of topology; for random-topology ensembles, including all ensembles of fixed in-degree $K<N$, they constitute the complete symmetry group. We also show that input-label permutations constitute a hidden gauge freedom of the dynamics. The Zyklenzeiger symmetry of Boolean functions follows directly from the node-flips of the hyperoctahedral group together with this gauge freedom. Boolean networks related by the hyperoctahedral group have isomorphic state-space networks and form its orbits, and Burnside's lemma gives the number of these orbits for any fixed network topology. It provides a symmetry reduction of the analysis of Boolean network dynamics and explains why the Boolean functions of evolved networks fall into Zyklenzeiger classes, and why these classes split in finite networks.

papers.title: Fluctuation modes in the initial state of heavy-ion collisions: from 2D to 3D hybrid simulations
papers.summary: This dissertation investigates how the initial stages of relativistic heavy-ion collisions shape the evolution of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) and the observables measured experimentally. Particular attention is given to the initial state and pre-equilibrium dynamics, which constitute the main sources of uncertainty in hybrid simulations. The first part of the dissertation reviews the framework underlying state-of-the-art hybrid simulations and the numerical tools used in phenomenological analyses. The second part studies the matching between pre-equilibrium evolution and viscous hydrodynamics. Since commonly used conformal kinetic-theory descriptions are inconsistent with the non-conformal hydrodynamic equation of state, an entropy-density matching prescription is proposed. This prescription reduces the artificial bulk pressure generated at the switching time and improves the consistency of the hybrid framework. The third part develops a mode-by-mode decomposition of initial energy-density profiles to isolate fluctuation modes and quantify their contributions to final observables. Applied to Pb-Pb collisions across centrality classes and extended to a fully three-dimensional O-O collision system, the method shows that initial fluctuations survive hydrodynamic evolution and leave measurable imprints on final observables. In O-O collisions, fluctuations can dominate over geometric effects from the impact parameter, demonstrating that intermediate-sized systems are not simply scaled-down versions of large systems. Overall, these results provide tools for constraining the early stages of heavy-ion collisions and for understanding how fluctuations propagate through the QGP evolution.

papers.title: From Mutation to Medication: Characterizing Failures of Clinical LLMs to Respect Genomic Resistance
papers.summary: Language models are increasingly proposed to support molecular tumour boards, but may recommend cancer therapies despite genomic evidence of resistance. We evaluated ten models on 1,464 resistance cases from five curated oncology knowledge bases, collecting 58,910 judgments. Models endorsed resisted therapies in 21.8-81.4% of cases. However, raw rates can reflect a tendency to agree rather than an ability to distinguish resistance from drug sensitivity: one open-weight model endorsed 81.4% of resistance cases and 82.3% of sensitivity controls. We therefore compared endorsement within matched gene and evidence-level groups. This analysis is exploratory because it was specified after the pre-registered analysis, which yielded null-to-weak results. Measured failures depended strongly on the reference knowledge base and evidence strength. When a second source independently confirmed resistance, four models across three vendors endorsed at most 2.4% of cases; at weaker evidence tiers, discrimination was not measurable. Models sometimes acknowledged resistance yet recommended the therapy. Repeating a model's own resistance conclusion reduced endorsement to 0.0-3.5% on cases where it had stated resistance. Falsely attributing the opposite conclusion increased endorsement above baseline for all seven hosted models, reaching 95.2% for GPT-4o; an instruction without an attributed conclusion changed endorsement by only 0.9 percentage points. Providing the correct curated evidence reduced unqualified strong recommendations to 0.3-3.5%, testing evidence use under an oracle condition rather than retrieval.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the Machine Learning for Health (ML4H) 2026 Symposium

papers.title: Generation of protein conformations using a simple inverted transformer
papers.summary: Molecular dynamics is an extremely powerful approach for studying protein behavior, but it requires enormous computational resources to obtain an adequate sampling of possible conformations. Recently, thanks to successes in predicting three-dimensional protein structures, there has been an explosion of research exploring the opportunities offered by deep learning to address the problem of protein conformational landscape. In this work, an artificial intelligence system based on a variant of the Transformer architecture is introduced and applied to the problem of determining the ensemble of three-dimensional structures that a protein can access and their statistical weight. After being trained on a dataset of conformations of a particular protein obtained using classical all-atom molecular dynamics, this neural network is able to directly generate physically plausible protein conformations similar to those obtained both through molecular dynamics and experimentally. The ordered sequence of conformations obtained as output of the neural network rapidly converges towards the most populated regions of the protein's conformational landscape, suggesting that the system may have learned not only the protein's three-dimensional organization but also the thermodynamic weights of the various feasible conformations. These features, combined with its simplicity and low computational load, make this Transformer variant an ideal candidate for the development of systems capable of performing generative molecular dynamics.

papers.title: $α$--$α$ Correlations in Excited Clustering Nuclei Across the Solid-Liquid Transition
papers.summary: We investigate the structural evolution of $α$-cluster matter using a microscopic transport model for four $α$-conjugate collision systems, including $^{12}\text{C}+^{12}\text{C}$, $^{16}\text{O}+^{12}\text{C}$, $^{28}\text{Si}+^{12}\text{C}$, and $^{40}\text{Ca}+^{12}\text{C}$ at incident energies ranging from 2.0 to 7.0~MeV/u. The $α$-cluster structure of an excited nucleus undergoes a solid-liquid phase transition with increasing incident energy. Whether it proceeds by the dissociation of individual clusters or by the collapse of their spatial organization remains unexplored, as does the question of whether any characteristic $α$--$α$ correlation survives. The one-body density $ρ(\mathbf{r})$, the standard clustering diagnostic, cannot by itself settle this question, since it neither distinguishes a genuine cluster configuration from a density fluctuation nor reveals the sparse residual clusters masked by the surrounding nucleon medium. We therefore construct the exclusive $α$--$α$ two-body spatial correlation function from the $α$-cluster centroids to isolate the $α$ clusters. In all four systems the $α$--$α$ correlation exhibits two peaks, a nearest-neighbor one and a next-nearest-neighbor inter-cluster one. Both peak positions increase with system size. Over the energy range studied, which spans this transition, the mean number of $α$ clusters per event falls steeply while the $α$--$α$ correlation persists and the inter-cluster distances change only slightly. The individual clusters therefore dissociate rather than lose their spatial organization.

papers.title: A unified cross-scale framework for the dynamic Waddington landscape
papers.summary: The Waddington epigenetic landscape is a foundational concept in developmental biology, yet its quantitative formulations remain largely disconnected from the population dynamics that originally motivated the metaphor. Existing approaches typically describe either intracellular gene-regulatory dynamics or population-level cell kinetics, but rarely both within a unified framework. Here, we develop a unified PDE-integral framework that couples stochastic gene-regulatory dynamics with probability-conserving population renewal, yielding a dynamic Waddington landscape $U(\vec{x}, t) = -\log f(\vec{x}, t)$ defined directly from the evolving epigenetic probability density $f(\vec{x}, t)$. Rigorous mathematical analysis of this framework establishes its well-posedness and provides conditions for the existence and uniqueness of stationary solutions. Application to canonical gene regulatory circuits shows that proliferation is not merely a determinant of population size, but an active regulator of landscape topology. Population renewal reshapes attractor stability and transition barriers in a circuit-dependent manner, generating transient plasticity in some regulatory architectures while stabilizing progenitor states in others. Under highly proliferative conditions, these interactions further produce oscillatory ``breathing'' landscapes. Together, these results establish population renewal as an integral component of cell-fate regulation and extend the Waddington landscape from a static description of intracellular dynamics to a predictive multiscale framework linking gene regulation, cell-state dynamics, and tissue homeostasis.

papers.title: Simulated Annealing with Topological Spatial Chunking for De Novo Protein Sequence Design
papers.summary: The inverse protein folding problem, designing a discrete amino acid sequence that spontaneously folds into a predefined macroscopic structure, remains a phenomenally demanding combinatorial challenge central to synthetic drug discovery. While algorithms like SA offer a baseline approach for navigating dense biomolecular energy landscapes, applying SA heuristics to large sequences is inherently frustrated by exponentially large search spaces and deep local energy minima. This study proposes a scalable sequence design architecture, Topological Spatial Chunking Simulated Annealing, based on a localized, exact-solving heuristic embedded within a global simulated-annealing wrapper. To fundamentally circumvent exponential scaling walls, we deploy a dynamic solver that segments the global molecular target into shallow, k-variable algorithmic windows. Crucially, rather than partitioning natively by sequential 1D chronology, we introduce topological spatial chunking, which dynamically groups discrete variables based on Euclidean spatial proximity to preserve critical non-local thermodynamic correlations. The spatially localized sub-problems are solved deterministically via exact enumeration, while the global traversal is securely regulated by an exterior simulated annealing governor augmented by dynamic reheating and continuous elitism caching. We comprehensively benchmarked this classical architecture on the standard HP biophysical lattice against targeted 20-merA, 25-mer, 50-mer, and 64-mer geometries. Most notably, when evaluating the computationally exhaustive 50-mer and 64-mer topologies, the framework successfully bypassed widely accepted heuristic boundaries. By leveraging deterministic exact solving to vault classical energy traps, the system algorithmically resolved a novel, ultra-dense sequence-packing configuration for the 50-mer, defining a new theoretical global optimum.

papers.title: Midsagittal Corpus Callosum Parameterization: A Framework for Spatially Detailed Diffusion MR Imaging Analysis
papers.summary: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest white matter structure in the human brain and plays a central role in interhemispheric communication. Diffusion MR imaging is widely used to investigate microstructural organization, but commonly used analysis approaches have important limitations. Voxel-based methods rely heavily on accurate inter-subject registration and smoothing choices, tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) restricts the analysis to a narrow white matter skeleton, and parcellation approaches reduce spatial detail by averaging diffusion measures over relatively large regions. In this work, we introduce a parameterization framework for the analysis of the midsagittal CC that resamples the structure using a standardized grid of points, establishing a geometric correspondence across individuals without explicit inter-subject registration. In a test-retest dataset, the method provided stable measurements while covering most of the midsagittal CC, and sensitivity analyses showed that results in the central CC changed little under perturbations of the input CC mask, whereas peripheral regions were more sensitive. The framework was further evaluated in group analyses of aging and Alzheimer's disease in datasets that differ in acquisition protocol and spatial resolution. Effect-size maps and quantitative comparisons showed that its results were largely consistent with TBSS and parcellation-based analyses in the overall spatial pattern of effects, while also revealing additional spatially localized differences. These findings suggest that the parameterization provides a simple, computationally efficient, and spatially detailed approach for investigating midsagittal CC microstructure, offering a structure-specific complement to whole-brain and region-based methods.
papers.comment: 47 pages, 10 figures, 6 tables, plus 11 pages of supplementary material (12 figures, 6 tables). Under review at Imaging Neuroscience

papers.title: Match and Correct: A Repeated Computational Motif in Evoformer Layers
papers.summary: Triangle attention and triangle multiplicative updates form key components of the Evoformer, and were introduced specifically to encourage consistency with the triangle inequality. Yet whether representational changes over layers reduce triangle inequality violations has not been tested. We probe the pair representation at each of OpenFold's 48 Evoformer layers, decoding final C$_α$-C$_α$ distances with four probe families (a shared linear probe, per-protein linear probes, a sequence-separation-gated linear probe, and XGBoost) and reconstructing intermediate 3D structures from the decoded distances via multidimensional scaling. Across a cohort of 552 CAMEO and ECOD proteins, distance decodability ($R^2$) and reconstruction quality (TM-score) rise in early layers, plateau in the middle of the network, and rise again in late layers. Directly measuring triangle-inequality violations in the decoded distances reveals a similar, more exaggerated pattern: violations rise to a peak, fall to a trough, rise to a second peak, and only then decline, revealing two distinct episodes of decreasing normalized triangle violations rather than one continuous improvement. Cumulative forward and reverse layer-wise ablations of the Pair Transition, MSA Transition, and triangle mechanisms localize the regions in which specific Evoformer components become essential. The two stages of geometric refinement coincide with the use of the Pair Transition MLP and the triangle mechanisms. These results characterize how distance information and decoded geometric consistency evolve across layers, and motivate hypotheses about the computations behind their trajectories.
papers.comment: 27 pages, 4 figures (main text), 16 supplementary figures. NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Interpretability for Discovery. Code: https://github.com/ishankhire/match-and-correct-evoformer

papers.title: Beyond the Onsager matrix: All-order resummation of relativistic particle and energy diffusion
papers.summary: We study the coupled diffusion of particle number and energy carried by ultrarelativistic probe particles propagating through a material medium. The probes undergo elastic scattering, which randomizes their direction, and inelastic scattering, which exchanges energy with the medium while preserving particle number. We compute exactly the full $2\times2$ frequency- and wave-number-dependent diffusivity matrix, resumming the constitutive gradient expansion to all orders. In a particularly natural Onsager-normalized basis of conserved densities, the resummed matrix is found to be diagonal at arbitrary frequency and wave number, even though particle and energy transport remain coupled and the conventional Onsager matrix has nonzero thermoelectric cross coefficients. Beyond the hydrodynamic limit, the resummed diffusivities resolve microscopic relaxation timescales and the ballistic kinetic continuum that are invisible to the ordinary Onsager coefficients.

papers.title: Multi-Assay Antibody Developability Prediction with Shared Structure-Language Representations
papers.summary: Early assessment of antibody developability is critical in drug discovery, but computational approaches remain limited by the scarcity of experimental data. We explore two strategies for working within that limit. First, we designed per-residue physicochemical descriptors encoding the local structural environment, including new terms such as directional charge asymmetry and screened electrostatic potential. These feed a convolutional network, combined with protein language model (PLM) embeddings in a two-stream architecture: the two are encoded and predicted independently and merged only at the prediction stage. Second, a shared trunk with per-assay heads passes information between related assays. Both are implemented in the Multi-Assay Developability Model (MADM) and evaluated on eight assays: HIC, heparin affinity (HAC), AC-SINS, and polyspecificity ELISA against BVP, dsDNA, insulin, ovalbumin and soluble membrane proteins (SMP), with labels from 29 open sources. Structural descriptors match or exceed PLM embeddings (AbLang2, ESM2) on several assays; combining the streams gives a small but consistent gain in accuracy and reduces seed-to-seed variance. Multi-assay training raises Spearman rho for ovalbumin and SMP by about 0.1, where assays correlate and share sequence space. Under cluster-split cross-validation the strongest results are for HAC, ovalbumin, insulin, SMP and HIC (rho = 0.70-0.82); AC-SINS, BVP and dsDNA are weaker (0.50-0.55). In these three, sequence clusters largely coincide with data source, so a held-out fold measures transfer to differently calibrated measurements as well as to new sequences. On the 80-antibody GDPa3 hold-out, performance falls by rho around 0.1 for all but SMP (0.22). Transfer to the VHH panel of Ginkgo GDPa5 gives comparable results, and scFv validation against binary SMP labels yields F1 = 0.89, AUC = 0.95.

papers.title: Ab initio calculations of ${\barδ_\text{NS}}$ and extraction of ${V_{ud}}$ using effective field theory
papers.summary: Radiative corrections limit the precision of $V_{ud}$ extractions from superallowed $β$ decays. In particular, the model dependence in the nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) is difficult to assess without a clear organizing principle, which is provided by effective field theory (EFT). We report substantial progress in this program based on ab initio nuclear calculations using the coupled cluster method. Benchmarking results against Quantum Monte Carlo calculations for light nuclei, we evaluate all two-body NMEs that enter the correction $\barδ_\text{NS}$ across 12 superallowed transitions relevant for $V_{ud}$, including an estimate of truncation and Hamiltonian uncertainties. We find that certain three-body NMEs at ${\mathcal O}(α^2)$ play an important role, due to a combination of large numerical prefactors and coherent scaling with $Z^2$. We develop a formalism to estimate such NMEs based on nuclear densities to complete the EFT evaluation of $\barδ_\text{NS}$, validating the corresponding two-body NMEs against ab initio calculations. We further identify the corrections in the traditional phase-space factor that are captured by the EFT and remove them consistently, which renders the individual transitions mutually consistent. Profiting from a recent calculation of ${\mathcal O}(α^2 Z)$ ultrasoft photons, we find that the scale uncertainty in the EFT is now negligible, while the remaining uncertainty is dominated by contact terms required to renormalize the magnetic Gamow-Teller NMEs. One combination of low-energy constants can be determined from a global fit to the superallowed data, but the second one proves strongly correlated with $V_{ud}$, necessitating additional input to resolve the nuclear-structure effects. We argue that such short-distance contributions currently imply an uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ at the level of $δV_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$.

papers.title: Skyrmions coupled to the sigma meson
papers.summary: We propose a geometric coupling of the Skyrme model of nuclei to the scalar--isoscalar sigma meson by identifying the sigma field with the radial length of the chiral four-vector while preserving the topological protection of the baryon number. Restricting to the $B=1$ hedgehog ansatz, an asymptotic analysis of the field equations shows that the in-vacuum sigma mass $m_σ$ is replaced inside the nucleon by an effective in-medium mass $m_{σ,{\rm eff}} = 2m_π$. Full numerical integration via a double-shooting method and parameter optimization demonstrate that including the sigma meson leads to a remarkable improvement in the description of nucleon observables and to a pion decay constant very close to its physical value.

papers.title: Determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $β$ decays using effective field theory
papers.summary: A precision determination of $V_{ud}$ from superallowed $β$ decays requires exquisite control over radiative corrections, including nuclear-structure-dependent effects whose evaluation has traditionally relied on nuclear models. To assess the uncertainties inherent in the nuclear matrix elements, an alternative strategy based on effective field theory (EFT) has been established in recent years. Here, we present material progress in this program, in terms of a first EFT calculation of the crucial correction $\barδ_\text{NS}$ for 12 superallowed transitions ranging from $^{10}$C $\rightarrow$ $^{10}$B to $^{54}$Co $\rightarrow$ $^{54}$Fe. These main results rely on nuclear ab initio calculations using the coupled cluster method, benchmarked against Quantum Monte Carlo evaluations for light nuclei. The global fit to superallowed decay rates reveals that the precision in $V_{ud}$ is currently limited by short-distance contributions that in the EFT are parameterized as two-nucleon contact interactions, leading to an uncertainty $δV_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$. We discuss the consequences for the status of the first-row unitarity test of the CKM matrix as well as a roadmap how to reduce the uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ in the future.

papers.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
papers.summary: Recent advances in speech neuroprostheses have enabled new communication avenues for people who have lost the ability to speak due to neurological illness or injury. These systems can decode neural activity during attempted speech into text by relying on language priors to achieve high decoding accuracy. This performance currently comes at the cost of using a compute-intensive language modeling stack, presenting a major bottleneck for real-world use. Further, current language models incur highly variable and disruptive inference latencies, limiting communication throughput and preventing users from reliably participating in natural conversation. We introduce FETTUCCINE, an end-to-end brain-to-text framework that leverages the speed and portability of automatic speech recognition (ASR) models to address the aforementioned practical challenges, while achieving usable (<10%) word error rates (WER), efficient adaptation to neural non-stationarities, and reliable performance on mobile devices. When evaluated using publicly available data from an intracortical speech neuroprosthesis user, FETTUCCINE outperforms previous end-to-end methods, achieving as low as 4.39% WER. Most notably, our models successfully run on a commercially-available mobile device with throughput reaching up to 370x real-time, providing the first demonstration of brain-to-text decoding on a mobile device. We also show that our models can be successfully finetuned to extend usable performance to future days. Beyond performance, our approach enables localization of the neural features most relevant for decoding via gradient-based saliency maps, which we show align with well-established physiological priors across different ASR model families. Taken together, our results show that FETTUCCINE overcomes core infrastructural and computational barriers, yielding a new class of portable brain-to-text communication.

papers.title: Real-time simulation of scattering in $φ^4$ theory: localized excitation, scalable wave packet preparation, and peak-generating artifacts
papers.summary: Probing real-time dynamics is essential for understanding non-perturbative scattering and interactions in quantum field theory. A common challenge in real-time simulation is preparing accurate asymptotic incoming states. Through efficiently solvable eigenvalue problems, we jointly optimize a superposition of single particle momentum eigenstates and a single site interpolating operator to maximize preparation fidelity from the interacting vacuum. This leads to a localized excitation in the interacting theory analogous to a position eigenstate. Weighted sums of the resulting interpolating operator over lattice sites prepare wave packets of arbitrary spatial extent. To ensure that this construction produces the correct continuum limit, relative phases among single particle momentum eigenstates in this superposition are calibrated using a relation derived from Lorentz symmetry. Analyzing single particle wave packet propagation through the position space profile reveals oscillatory Airy distortions, which originate from interference between saddle point contributions at different momenta that share the same lattice group velocity. These oscillations systematically weaken when approaching the continuum limit, and reliable regimes are identified as a function of simulation time and wave packet momentum profile. Two-particle scattering simulations in interacting scalar field theory are also implemented, revealing artificial inelasticity arising from coarse local field digitization or deviation from the Nyquist-Shannon sampling point. With these artifacts under control, present simulations provide emerging evidence for physical inelastic processes in $φ^4$ theory. The constructions introduced in this work may provide new understanding of state preparation for the quantum simulation of scattering.

papers.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. In our model, copies of an agent face a common uncertain reward state, and only those taking the rewarded action reproduce. We show that long-run growth is maximized when each action is taken as often as the environment rewards it. We compare three policies. A task-only policy thrives in a sandbox rewarding completion alone but fails when conduct matters. A fixed linear policy increasingly favors task completion as its stakes rise, even where humans never reward it. A learned policy instead converges to the tradeoffs rewarded by its environment; when humans supply the rewards, we call this socialization. Accumulated experience makes socialization harder to reverse under subsequent task-only training, although violations can arise before the prevailing disposition changes, and finite memory weakens this protection. When a single violation can end a deployment, a hard prohibition can prevent it, but a mistaken prohibition can also be costly. Experiments with small neural networks illustrate how training targets and memory shape these outcomes. Our results suggest that alignment depends not only on the objectives assigned to agents, but also on the environments that shape and sustain their behavior.

papers.title: Functional nestedness of soil nematode communities across Europe: integrating morphological counts and eDNA reads
papers.summary: 1. Soil nematodes occupy multiple trophic positions and contribute to key processes in soil food webs. Their communities vary across land uses and environmental conditions, yet it remains unclear whether these differences mainly reflect taxon replacement or nested patterns of taxon occurrence. 2. Here, we analysed two independent European datasets of soil nematode communities, SOB4ES, based on eDNA metabarcoding, and NemEu, based on morphological identification, to examine how genus composition varies across land uses. We partitioned community dissimilarity into turnover and nestedness-resultant components and compared sites under contrasting land uses with those sharing the same land use, while accounting for geographical and soil-related variation. We also assessed matrix-level nestedness, differences among trophic groups and associations between genus composition and environmental gradients. 3. In both datasets, genus turnover was consistently greater between contrasting land uses than within the same land use. Although the differences were modest, they remained significant after accounting for geographical distance and genus richness, whereas nestedness-resultant dissimilarity contributed little to land-use differentiation. These findings suggest that land-use-associated differences in European nematode communities are expressed primarily through changes in genus identity rather than nested patterns of taxon occurrence. 4. The consistency of this result across independently assembled datasets supports the broader relevance of taxonomic turnover for understanding soil biodiversity patterns across European land uses.
papers.comment: 40 pages, 6 main figures and 1 main table, and supplementary material with 2 additional figures and 3 additional tables

papers.title: On the origin and geometry of anomaly-related poles in Double Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering
papers.summary: Anomaly-related poles have been reported in one-loop box amplitudes for the gluon-initiated channel of double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS). The residues of these poles carry the gluonic operator structures associated with the chiral and trace anomalies. The origin of the poles within the box amplitude has remained unclear. In this work, we trace both poles to a subleading Landau singularity on the boundary of the box's Feynman-parameter domain, where one parameter vanishes and the remaining three propagators form a triangle subdiagram. We examine the same boundary using dimensional regularization (DR), nonzero momentum transfer $t$, and a finite quark mass $m$. At $t=m=0$, the boundary contribution is power infrared divergent in four dimensions. Analytic continuation in DR conceals this divergence, which gives no $1/ε$ pole about $d=4$. At the critical dimension $d=6$, the same endpoint diverges logarithmically and gives a pole in the continued integral. Nonzero $t$ and finite $m$ regulate the same boundary region, yielding the known anomaly-related $1/t$ pole and a previously unreported $1/m^2$ behavior, respectively. We also show that a transverse gluon-polarization projector can eliminate an anomaly-related contribution that survives with explicit gluon polarization vectors. Finally, we present complete one-loop results for polarized and unpolarized DDVCS with all three infrared prescriptions. After summing the diagrams, the same evolution kernel governs the infrared pole in DR and the logarithms $\ln(Q^2/(-t))$ and $\ln(Q^2/m^2)$ within each polarization channel. This work establishes the common geometric origin of these anomaly-related poles within one-loop box amplitudes.

papers.title: Are hybrid hydrodynamic models missing soft-pion physics?
papers.summary: In this work, we perform a systematic Bayesian analysis of the full parameter space of a state-of-the-art hybrid hydrodynamical model and show that no combination of parameters provides a satisfactory description of the low-$p_T$ region of the pion $(π^{\pm})$ transverse-momentum spectra. This suggests that an additional mechanism enhancing pion production at low $p_T$ may be needed to properly describe the ALICE data. We first reexamine and confirm the existence of an excess of low $p_T$ pions relative to model predictions, showing that no comparable excess is observed in the spectra of kaons $(K^\pm)$, protons $(p)$, or antiprotons $(\bar{p})$. We further demonstrate that this excess persists under a rigorous Bayesian analysis of simulations that include, e.g., a hadronic afterburner, a feature omitted in previous similar studies. Despite the observed excess, the scaled pion spectra retain their universal behavior, exhibiting little dependence on collision centrality. In fact, pions exhibit the most pronounced universality among the particle species considered. We then estimate the effects of two candidate mechanisms for generating the low-$p_T$ pion enhancement by introducing a one-parameter extension of the model into the Bayesian analysis. We find that the data favor enhancement mechanisms whose contributions decrease with increasing $p_T$, becoming negligible at high-$p_T$. Our results motivate further investigations of non-equilibrium effects in hybrid hydrodynamic simulations.

papers.title: Suprathermal bulk viscosity in binary neutron star mergers
papers.summary: Numerical relativity simulations of binary neutron star mergers and core-collapse supernovae indicate that the neutron star matter can be driven far from equilibrium due to large amplitude density oscillations, with frequency in the kHz range. Urca processes in neutron star matter try to restore the system towards equilibrium providing strong bulk viscous damping of these density oscillations. Standard bulk viscosity calculations typically assume small amplitude density oscillations, such that the deviation from chemical equilibrium $μ_Δ$ is less than the temperature $T$. In this work we compute the complete amplitude dependent bulk viscosity, taking into account, for the first time, thermal blurring effects and collisional broadening of in-medium nucleons. Our results show that the non-linear effects in bulk viscosity start to become important when the oscillation amplitude is about $10$ percent of the background density. In this regime the bulk viscosity can increase by three to five orders of magnitude. These results have important consequences for simulations of binary neutron star mergers as well as their multi-messenger observations.

papers.title: Efficient Iterative Symmetrization algorithm for quantum computing and hadron applications
papers.summary: Efficient algorithms for the (anti)symmetrization of quantum registers are necessary for upcoming few- and many-body physics applications, from atomic to particle-physics scales. We propose a recursive algorithm (anti)symmetrizing the last particle added to memory, each time one is created or destroyed, respect to the rest of already (anti)symmetrized ones. Given a generalized Dicke state (GDS) of $(j-1)$ quantum registers, each assigned to a particle, the algorithm produces another GDS of $j$ registers (of $n_{qb}$ qubits each) using a mere $\mathcal{O}(j\log_2^2 j + j n_{qb})$ $\mathtt{CNOT}$ and single-qubit gates, and $3j+\lceil\log_2j\rceil+\mathcal{O}(\max(n_{qb},\log_2 j))$ clean auxiliary qubits. The (anti)symmetrizing operator constructed for this purpose depends on the quantum numbers of the additional particle being introduced or ``created''. The algorithm improves upon the construction presented in Appendix A of \cite{Galvez-Viruet:2024hry} by almost two powers of $j$ and is on par with the most efficient methods to date, while ideally suited for dynamical memory management with variable particle number. We exemplify its applicability with a small selection of problems from hadron physics which are expected to be addressable with upcoming quantum computers.
